MAPPING: per my_fir instance (taps x0=din, x1..x6=n_delay_reg1..6, nd=new_data_rdy): clk=clk, reset=1'b0, mode_sigs=12'b0, chainin=37'b0, chainout unconnected; ax={1'b0,(nd?din:n_delay_reg1)+(nd?n_delay_reg4:n_delay_reg5)} (= x1+x5 of the next cycle), ay=19'd c1, bx={1'b0,(nd?n_delay_reg1:n_delay_reg2)+(nd?n_delay_reg3:n_delay_reg4)} (= x2+x4 of the next cycle), by=19'd c2, result[27:0] -> the module's dout sum. Coefficients (c0,c1,c2,c3): f1 29,101,15,235; f2 4,42,163,255; f3 12,77,148,-; h1 15,25,193,-; h2 4,42,163,255; h3 9,56,109,-; h4 9,56,109,-. The c0/c6 pair and the c3 term stay in soft logic as registered shift-adds t0 and t3; dout = result[27:0] + t0 + t3.
PLAN:

1. What is converted, and why this shape

Every my_fir module (f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4; 6 instances each, 42 instances) gets exactly one int_sop_2. The four products whose coefficients are c1, c2, c4=c2, c5=c1 are folded by the filter's symmetry into the block's two product terms; the c0/c6 pair and the c3 term stay in soft logic.

Every my_fir coefficient set is symmetric (c0=c6, c1=c5, c2=c4): f1 29,101,15,235,15,101,29 (lines 1440-1449); f2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4 (1500-1506); f3 12,77,148,0,148,77,12 (1561-1567); h1 15,25,193,0,193,25,15 (1616-1625); h2 4,42,163,255,163,42,4 (1675-1681); h3 and h4 9,56,109,0,109,56,9 (1734-1740, 1792-1798). So

S(x) = c0*(x0+x6) + c1*(x1+x5) + c2*(x2+x4) + c3*x3

is the same integer as the original seven (or six) separate products summed, and every intermediate stays far below the 28-bit width of dout (worst case f2/h2: 65535*673 = 44,105,055 < 2^28), so the regrouping is bit-exact, not merely approximate. Each folded operand x_i+x_j is 17 bits (fits ax/bx[18]), each coefficient <= 255 (fits ay/by[19]), each block sum <= 34.6M (no wrap at 2^37).

Per-instance rewrite (same in all 42 instances)

Unchanged: the n_delay_reg1..6 enabled shift chain and output_data_ready. Added soft logic:

wire [15:0] xn1 = nd ? din          : n_delay_reg1;   // = x1 of the next cycle
wire [15:0] xn2 = nd ? n_delay_reg1 : n_delay_reg2;
wire [15:0] xn4 = nd ? n_delay_reg3 : n_delay_reg4;
wire [15:0] xn5 = nd ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg5;
wire [16:0] pa  = xn1 + xn5;                          // = x1+x5 of the next cycle
wire [16:0] pb  = xn2 + xn4;                          // = x2+x4 of the next cycle

These four muxes are the same expression that already drives the enabled delay registers, so the block's operand register becomes a shadow of the delay line one cycle ahead: the block's ax/bx register, loaded at the edge that ends cycle m-1, holds x1(m)+x5(m) and x2(m)+x4(m), and result during cycle m+1 is c1*(x1+x5)(m) + c2*(x2+x4)(m). This is what makes the block's fixed 2-cycle operand-to-result latency land on the cycle the original dout register landed on; feeding the block the register outputs directly would be one cycle late, and a transposed or chained form cannot be used (see section 4).

Soft registered terms, loaded from the current-cycle values (no mux needed, they are read in cycle m and used in cycle m+1), written as explicit shifts and adds so synthesis leaves them in soft logic rather than inferring another DSP:

t0 <= c0 * (din + n_delay_reg6);   // 29*s=(s<<5)-(s<<1)-s; 4*s=s<<2; 12*s=(s<<3)+(s<<2);
                                   // 15*s=(s<<4)-s; 9*s=(s<<3)+s       (t0 is [21:0])
t3 <= c3 * n_delay_reg3;           // f1: (n3<<8)-(n3<<4)-(n3<<2)-n3 ; f2,h2: (n3<<8)-n3
                                   // f3,h1,h3,h4: no t3                (t3 is [23:0])

All these subtractions stay non-negative at every step, so unsigned arithmetic is exact.

Output: dout changes from a 28-bit enabled register to a wire,

assign dout = result[27:0] + t0 + t3;      // t3 omitted in f3,h1,h3,h4

which during cycle m+1 equals S(x(m)) - exactly the value the original dout register held during cycle m+1 whenever new_data_rdy was 1 in cycle m.

Why dropping the enable on dout is behaviour-preserving

dout leaves my_fir only as vidin_out_temp_f1..h4 in h_fltr (lines 479-499, 514-520) and is read at exactly one place, lines 523-554, each under if (my_fir_rdy_* == 1'b1). output_data_ready is assigned unconditionally in both branches (lines 1485/1496 and the six copies), so rdy during cycle m+1 equals nd during cycle m. The original dout during cycle m+1 is nd(m) ? S(x(m)) : dout(m); the rewrite's dout is S(x(m)) always. They differ only on cycles where rdy = 0, and on those cycles h_fltr does not sample it. No other reader exists (checked the whole file for vidin_out_temp), so nothing else can see the difference. This is the regrouping that makes the rewrite T2 rather than T1.

Reset and power-up

reset is tied to 1'b0 on every block. The top-level reset reaches only the video/SRAM state machine (the single use at line 203 clears video_state, tm3_sram_adsp, horiz, vert); the whole filter datapath - the fifos, fltr_compute, my_fir, h_fltr, steer_fltr, port_bus - has no reset. Driving the block's reset from it would clear the block's operand and result registers on a reset the original design does not react to, and the testbench pulses reset low mid-run while data flows (drive_sv2_top.vh lines 8 and 28), so the block's result would be wrong for two cycles after each pulse while the reference kept computing. Tying reset to 0 is the only driver under which "same behaviour holds after every reset".

With reset low the block's registers are overwritten every edge, so the power-up unknown is transient and provably never escapes: at the first clock edge the operand registers take real data (all design registers start at 0, all strobe inputs are driven) and result takes f(unknown) = X; at the second edge result takes f(0) = 0. dout is therefore X only during cycle 1, and rdy during cycle 1 equals nd during cycle 0, which is 0 because v_nd_s*_* (lines 430-441) are design registers that start at 0 and only load 1 at the first edge. So h_fltr does not sample cycle 1, and the first sample it does take (cycle 2) is already clean. The new soft registers t0/t3 also start unknown and are likewise clean from cycle 1 onward and never sampled before that.

No assumption about the design's inputs is needed; there is no ASSUMES line.

2. Regions left, with reasons

All 46 fltr_compute candidates (fltr_compute_f1 lines 859-865, f2 889-895, f3 928-934, h1 959-965, h2 992-998, h3 1030-1036, h4 1065-1071) are left, for two reasons, either of which is sufficient:

  • Power-up. fltr_compute has no gate anywhere on its output path: q1..q7, d_out_tmp and dout all load every cycle, and dout feeds my_fir's din, which is captured into the enabled delay line from the first strobe. A block there would push its unknown first-cycle result into dout, then into n_delay_reg1..6 where it survives six strobes, and on through h_fltr/steer_fltr/port_bus to bus_word_3..6 well inside the compared window. Clearing it at power-up needs the block's reset, and that reset can only come from the top-level reset, which the testbench also pulses mid-run - which the original, having no reset on this datapath, does not reproduce.
  • Tiles. These products pack four to a DSP tile and occupy 57 tiles in total. A block takes a tile alone; even folded 2:1 by the same symmetry these filters have, the seven modules need 2 blocks per instance, 84 tiles against 57, a net +27 tiles. The soft logic it would recover (the 7x17-bit q registers, the 20-bit d_out_tmp and the six-adder chain, against three 9-bit pre-adds, one 20-bit adder and a 2-bit sign-fold correction) is worth roughly the same, so this part of the trade is close to neutral while the power-up hazard is not.

my_fir c0/c6 products - $154 and $165 (f1), $169 and $180 (f2), $184 and $193 (f3), $197 and $206 (h1), $210 and $221 (h2), $225 and $234 (h3), $238 and $247 (h4) - are left in soft logic. The c0 term multiplies din, a wire into the module, not a tap of the delay line, so its cycle-m value cannot be presented to a block one cycle early the way the taps can; a block fed with din would deliver c0*din(m-1) when c0*din(m) is wanted. Folded with its symmetric partner c6*x6 into t0 = c0*(din+n_delay_reg6) it costs at most two soft adders (zero for f2/h2, where c0 = 4 is a shift).

my_fir c3 products - $159 (f1, x235), $174 (f2, x255), $215 (h2, x255) - are left in soft logic. The one block per instance is already filled by the two folded pairs, and a second block would spend a whole DSP tile (about 91 BLE-equivalents at 253779 against 27905 per 10-BLE cluster) to save 24 LUTs (x255 = (n3<<8)-n3) or 72 LUTs (x235 = (n3<<8)-(n3<<4)-(n3<<2)-n3). f3, h1, h3 and h4 have c3 = 0 and no such term at all.

3. Blocks, tiles, and the longest series of blocks

42 blocks are added, one per my_fir instance. No block drives another: chainin is tied to 37'b0 on all 42 and chainout is left unconnected, so the longest series of blocks in any stage is one, and no stage pays the 2.200 ns chainout path or a block-to-block hop. The one stage that contains a block is the block's own internal stage, 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns, well under the 11.6069 ns baseline critical path and under the 7.5 ns stage the rewrite leaves.

Tiles: the baseline's 224 tiles are the 57 that hold only the 9x9 fltr_compute products plus the 167 that hold the 270 two_mult_18x19 my_fir products (the design has no other multiply). All 270 of those products leave the tiles - 168 of them into the 42 blocks as 84 folded block products, the other 102 into soft shift-adds - so the design then uses 57 + 42 = 99 DSP tiles, 125 fewer than the baseline and far inside the device's 306. At 253779 per tile that is about -3.17e7 of hard-block area; the added soft logic (four 16-bit muxes, two 17-bit pre-adds, the t0/t3 shift-adds and one or two 28-bit output adders per instance, against the six- or five-adder chain and the 28-bit dout register that go away) is about +2100 BLEs, roughly +5.8e6, for a net area near 7.1e7 against the baseline 9.73e7.

4. Stages: what leaves, what arrives, and the slowest one

What leaves the slowest stage. The baseline's slowest stage (11.6069 ns, my_fir_f1: hard multiply, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop) and the second (11.293 ns, my_fir_f2, same shape) are both inside my_fir, and so is the same shape in all 42 instances. The whole adder chain and the dout register are removed from every one of them, so that stage ceases to exist across the design rather than merely getting shorter - which is why all seven my_fir modules are converted and not just the two named paths.

What arrives, with the sampled medians (register clk-Q 0.060, wire into soft logic 0.960, soft adder/LUT level 1.069, wire register-to-block 1.419, block input setup 0.019):

  • operand stage, delay register -> mux -> pre-add -> block input register: 0.060 + 0.960 + 1.069 + 1.069 + 1.419 + 0.019 = 4.60 ns (the longest stage the rewrite creates);
  • block internal stage: 2.219 ns;
  • soft product stage, din/n_delay_reg3 -> at most three shift-add levels -> t0/t3 register: 0.060 + 0.960 + 3 x 1.069 = 4.25 ns (f1 only; 2 levels or fewer elsewhere);
  • output stage, block result -> at most two 28-bit adders -> the enabled vidin_out_reg_* in h_fltr: 0.060 + 0.960 + 2 x 1.069 = 3.16 ns.

None of these touches 7.5 ns, and none of them lengthens a stage that the rewrite does not already shorten.

The slowest stage the rewrite leaves is then the untouched d_out_tmp stage of fltr_compute (lines 867, 897, 936, 967, 1000, 1038, 1073): the seven sign-extended 17-bit q registers summed in a six-adder chain, 0.060 + 0.960 + 6 x 1.069 + 0.019 = 7.45 ns, reported as 7.5. It has no multiply in it, which is why it sits about 4 ns under the baseline's my_fir stage. Other untouched candidates are shorter: steer_fltr's four-term im_p_tmp/im_n_tmp (lines 641, 643) is three adder levels, about 4.2 ns, and the fltr_compute multiply stage is one multiply into q, about 3.5 ns.

So the objective moves as area 9.73e7 -> about 7.1e7, delay 11.6069 -> about 7.5 ns, with wirelength expected to fall as well (125 fewer DSP tiles shrinks the placement's footprint, and 42 six-deep 28-bit adder chains are gone), against a modest rise in soft nets.

5. Register stages, before and after, for each converted region

Identical for all 28 converted ids, since every one sits in a my_fir dout sum:

  • Before: the product is combinational out of the DSP tile and is summed in the same cycle; one register stage from the operands (din, n_delay_reg1..6, read during cycle m) to the result (dout, valid during cycle m+1). This is the "products registered 0 stage(s) before the sum" row of the candidate table.
  • After: two register stages inside the block, its operand register and its result register. The operand register is loaded one cycle earlier than the tap it shadows, from the same next-value expression that drives the enabled delay register, so operands read during cycle m-1 give result during cycle m+1 and the module's output still presents S(x(m)) during cycle m+1. Externally the latency is unchanged at one cycle; dout's own 28-bit register is removed, and the two block registers replace it plus the enabled shift stage's duplicate. The soft terms t0/t3 keep one register stage, cycle m to cycle m+1, matching the block's result.

DESIGN_CHANGE: give the filter datapath a synchronous reset from the existing top-level reset - at least fltr_compute's q1..q7, d_out_tmp and dout (lines 856-869 and the six copies) and my_fir's n_delay_reg1..6 and output_data_ready. The block's reset could then be driven from the same signal and stay behaviour-preserving on the mid-run pulses as well as at power-up, which removes the blocker on the 46 fltr_compute candidates: each fltr_compute is symmetric too and folds onto 2 blocks per instance, deleting its 7x17-bit q registers, its 20-bit d_out_tmp and the six-adder chain that becomes the critical path after this rewrite (7.45 ns), at a cost of +27 DSP tiles.

1	// int_sop_2: result = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin, unsigned, modulo 2^37 (the sum wraps at the
2	// result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37] in; result[37],
4	// chainout[37] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (ax, ay, bx, by and chainin alike); the products
7	// and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (operands and
10	// chainin to chainout 1).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_2 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [17:0] ax, input [18:0] ay,
21	    input [17:0] bx, input [18:0] by,
22	    input [36:0] chainin,
23	    output reg [36:0] result,
24	    output [36:0] chainout
25	);
26	
27	    // stage 1: the input registers
28	    reg [17:0] ax_reg, bx_reg;
29	    reg [18:0] ay_reg, by_reg;
30	    reg [36:0] chainin_reg;
31	
32	    // combinational middle: the two products and their sum, from the registers
33	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 18x19 -> 37, exact
34	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
35	    wire [36:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + chainin_reg;          // modulo 2^37
36	
37	    always @(posedge clk) begin
38	        if (reset) begin
39	            result <= 0;
40	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
41	        end
42	        else begin
43	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by; chainin_reg <= chainin;
44	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
45	        end
46	    end
47	
48	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
49	
50	endmodule

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_2 (precision INT19)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37]
  • output ports: result[37], chainout[37]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 37 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 37 bits (modulo 2^37), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.
The design

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (channel width 300, median of five seeds, 1 to 5) has a worst register-to-register path of 11.6069 ns on its one clock tm3_clk_v0 (I/O pads not timed) and uses 224 DSP tiles (as packed at seed 1) of the device's 306. Its used logic-block area is 9.73358e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905) and its routed wirelength is 436921, so its area x delay x wirelength product, the objective, is 4.93619e+14. Its slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report) is in my_fir_f1: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report), in my_fir_f2 (endpoint group $dffe~642, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1, one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 11.293 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • Blocks in series are separate stages. A path through chainout starts at an input register and continues, in the same stage, into what it drives.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's chainout can drive the next block's chainin directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

PLAN:

1. What is kept, what is new

The kept candidate (42 my_fir blocks) is reproduced unchanged; this revision adds the conversion of the seven fltr_compute_* modules, whose q1..q7 -> d_out_tmp stage is exactly the stage that the measurement reports as the new critical path (6 adder levels, $add~1634..1639, 7.576 ns at seed 1: a latch clock-to-Q, six 20-bit carry chains with ~1.0 ns of wire between them, 1.599 ns into $dff~1653). That stage disappears entirely.

Apply both parts to the unmodified source.

2. Part A — my_fir (reproduce the kept candidate exactly)

For each of my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h2, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4:

3. Part B — fltr_compute (new)

The seven coefficient sets are symmetric (c1=c7, c2=c6, c3=c5), so the seven products fold into four: c1*(d1+d7), c2*(d2+d6), c3*(d3+d5), c4*d4. Every product is exact in its 17-bit q register (the largest is 364*255 = 92820 < 2^17), so folding a symmetric pair into one product of the 9-bit pre-sum reproduces the pair's contribution bit for bit.

The one subtlety is the original's sign extension {q[16],q[16],q[16],q} of an unsigned product: for every i with q_i[16]=1 the 20-bit sum gets -2^17, i.e.

d_out_tmp = (sum of the seven exact products + 20'hE0000 * K) mod 2^20, K = #{ i : q_i >= 65536 },

and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3], so the correction may be added into a value wider than 20 bits and sliced at [18:3]. Only three coefficient sets can reach bit 16: f1 (277*d4, K = [d4 >= 237]), h4 (324*d4, K = [d4 >= 203]), f3 (364*d3 and 364*d5, K = [d3 >= 181] + [d5 >= 181]). For f2, h1, h2, h3 the largest product is 255*255 = 65025 < 65536, so K = 0 and no correction exists. Where a correction is needed it costs no adder: the soft term is below 2^17, so 20'hE0000*K mod 2^20 is just the three top bits of that 20-bit term (K=0 -> 3'b000, K=1 -> 3'b111, K=2 -> 3'b110).

Two products go on the block; the one or two cheap-coefficient products stay soft as shift-adds, split over the two register stages so that no stage holds more than two adder levels.

Replace each module body as follows (common head in every one of the seven):

verilog
    wire[7:0] d1 = din[55:48];  wire[7:0] d2 = din[47:40];  wire[7:0] d3 = din[39:32];
    wire[7:0] d4 = din[31:24];  wire[7:0] d5 = din[23:16];  wire[7:0] d6 = din[15:8];
    wire[7:0] d7 = din[7:0];
    wire[8:0] pa = d1 + d7;     wire[8:0] pb = d2 + d6;     wire[8:0] pc = d3 + d5;
    wire[36:0] sop_result;

and delete q1..q7 and d_out_tmp (nothing outside the module reads them; dout stays a 16-bit register).

fltr_compute_f1 (29,101,17,277) — block: 101*pb + 277*d4; soft: 29*pa + 17*pc + correction.

verilog

        .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd101), .bx({10'b0, d4}), .by(19'd277),
        .chainin(37'b0), .result(sop_result), .chainout());
    reg b1; reg[8:0] u; reg[16:0] v; reg[19:0] t;
    wire[16:0] u17 = u;  wire[16:0] pc17 = pc;
    wire[16:0] tlow = ((u17 << 5) + v) - (u17 + (u17 << 1));	// 29*pa + 17*pc, <= 23460

Note for the editor: every shift-add is written against a 17-bit wire (u17, pc17, s17) so no shift truncates; keep those widenings.

4. Every candidate, converted or left
  • my_fir_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (42 instances, 7 modules). Converted, as in the kept candidate: the COEF1 pair and the COEF2 pair of each filter (4 of the 6 or 7 products of each sum — the ids listed in REGIONS). Left in each: the COEF0/COEF6 pair and, where present, the COEF3 product — they stay soft because the block holds only two products and one block per my_fir instance is already a whole DSP tile; these coefficients (4, 9, 12, 15, 29, 235, 255) are one- to three-term shift-adds, cheaper than a second tile.
  • fltr_compute_f1 (lines 859-865) and fltr_compute_h4 (1065-1071). Converted: the c2 pair (860/864, 890-style 1066/1070) and the centre product (862, 1068). Left: the c1 pair (859/865, 1065/1071) and the c3 pair (861/863, 1067/1069) — their coefficients (29 and 17; 14 and 80) are one- and two-term shift-adds, so a second block (a whole tile per instance, 6 tiles per module) would cost more area than the ~35 soft BLEs they take; split over two register stages they add no more than two adder levels to any stage.
  • fltr_compute_f2 (889-895) and fltr_compute_h2 (992-998). Converted: the c2 pair (890/894, 993/997) and the c3 pair (891/893, 994/996). Left: the c1 pair (889/895, 992/998) and the centre (892, 995) — coefficient 4 is a shift and 255 is one subtract.
  • fltr_compute_f3 (928-934). Converted: the c2 pair (929/933) and the c3 pair (930/932). Left: the c1 pair (928/934), coefficient 20 = one add. (q4 is din*0 and is not a candidate.)
  • fltr_compute_h1 (959-965). Converted: 960/964 (25) and 961/963 (193). Left: 959/965, coefficient 17 = one add.
  • fltr_compute_h3 (1030-1036). Converted: 1030/1036 (23) and 1032/1034 (147). Left: 1031/1035, coefficient 72 = one add.

No candidate is left for a correctness reason; every left product is left because its coefficient is cheaper as a shift-add than a second DSP tile.

5. Blocks, tiles, and the stages
  • Blocks added: 84 — one per my_fir instance (42) and one per fltr_compute instance (42). No block is chained: every chainin is 37'b0, every chainout is unconnected, so the longest series of blocks in any stage is one block, 2.219 ns (0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019), well under the slowest stage.
  • DSP tiles after the rewrite: 84 (down from 99 in the kept candidate and 224 in the baseline). The 57 tiles that now hold the fltr_compute 9x9 products disappear: every remaining fltr multiply is an explicit shift-add. DSP area 84 x 253779 = 2.13e7, i.e. 3.8e6 below the kept candidate's, with the soft logic removed on top of that (per fltr_compute instance: seven 17-bit q registers and six 20-bit adder levels out, three 9-bit pre-adders, ~30 pipeline flip-flops, at most two shift-add levels and one 20-bit final adder in).
  • Soft logic leaving the slowest stage. The stage that leaves is exactly the measured critical stage: in each fltr_compute instance the 119 q flip-flops and the six-level 20-bit adder chain into d_out_tmp (7.576 ns at seed 1) are gone. What replaces them, per instance, is three stages of at most two adder levels each: (a) buff_out registers -> 9-bit pre-add -> block input register / stage-1 register (f1, h4: pre-add plus one shift-add level), about 0.06 + 1.0 + 1.07 + 1.6 = 3.8 ns at worst and 2.3 ns on the path into the block; (b) stage-1 registers -> at most two shift-add levels -> t, about 3.9 ns, running in parallel with the block's own 2.219 ns; (c) block result register -> one 20-bit add -> dout, about 0.06 + 0.96 + 1.07 + 1.6 = 3.7 ns. None of these is the slowest stage.
  • The slowest stage left is no longer in fltr_compute. The deepest remaining register-to-register stages are three-level soft chains elsewhere: my_fir's t3 <= (s3<<8)-(s3<<4)-(s3<<2)-s3 (three 26-bit levels) and steer_fltr's im_p_tmp/im_n_tmp (four 31-bit terms, three levels, lines 641 and 643). At the measured per-level cost of the seed-1 report (~1.07 ns a level plus ~1.6 ns into the endpoint register) that is about 5.0-5.3 ns, which is what STAGE_NS states. Both are untouched by this rewrite and neither is made slower by it.
6. Register stages, before and after
  • my_fir (unchanged from the kept candidate). Before: taps registered in the enabled delay chain, then one register (dout) over the whole products-and-sum, so operand to result was 1 stage with the multiply and six adder levels inside it. After: 2 stages (block input register, block result register), fed one cycle early from the same next-value expressions that drive the delay registers, so dout is produced on the cycle it was before; the soft t0/t3 terms take the matching single register stage and are added combinationally into dout.
  • fltr_compute (new). Before: 3 stages from din to dout — q1..q7 at edge k, d_out_tmp at edge k+1 (the six adder levels in between), dout at edge k+2. After: the same 3 stages — the block's input register at edge k (operands are the combinational pre-sums of din), the block's result register at edge k+1 (the two products and their sum in between, inside the block), dout at edge k+2 (one 20-bit add of result[19:0] and the soft term outside). The soft terms use the same two edges: a stage-1 register at edge k (u, v, s, and the comparison bits b1/b3/b5) and t at edge k+1. Operands applied before edge k therefore reach dout at edge k+2 exactly as in the original, cycle for cycle, and X-convergence after power-up is the same depth on both sides.
  • Reset: reset on every block is tied to 1'b0, as in the kept candidate. The design's reset (line 203, active low) touches only the video state machine; no register in fltr_compute or my_fir has a reset in the original, so tying the block's synchronous clear off keeps behaviour after every reset, not only at start-up. No rewrite register is relied on for an initial value.

No assumption about the design's inputs is needed: the rewrite is bit-exact for every input, including the original's sign extension of the unsigned 17-bit products, which is reproduced by the 20'hE0000 * K term in f1, f3 and h4 and is provably zero in f2, h1, h2 and h3.

DESIGN_CHANGE: in fltr_compute_* the seven products are unsigned but are summed as {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}, which subtracts 2^17 from the sum whenever a product reaches 65536 (only 277*d4, 324*d4 and 364*d3/d5 can). Widening q to 20 bits and zero-extending instead — or declaring the coefficients and q signed, which is what the commented-out negative coefficients suggest was meant — would remove the three comparators and the correction bits and let the sum go onto the block with nothing but the pre-adders outside it.

1	// int_sop_2: result = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin, unsigned, modulo 2^37 (the sum wraps at the
2	// result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37] in; result[37],
4	// chainout[37] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (ax, ay, bx, by and chainin alike); the products
7	// and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (operands and
10	// chainin to chainout 1).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_2 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [17:0] ax, input [18:0] ay,
21	    input [17:0] bx, input [18:0] by,
22	    input [36:0] chainin,
23	    output reg [36:0] result,
24	    output [36:0] chainout
25	);
26	
27	    // stage 1: the input registers
28	    reg [17:0] ax_reg, bx_reg;
29	    reg [18:0] ay_reg, by_reg;
30	    reg [36:0] chainin_reg;
31	
32	    // combinational middle: the two products and their sum, from the registers
33	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 18x19 -> 37, exact
34	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
35	    wire [36:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + chainin_reg;          // modulo 2^37
36	
37	    always @(posedge clk) begin
38	        if (reset) begin
39	            result <= 0;
40	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
41	        end
42	        else begin
43	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by; chainin_reg <= chainin;
44	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
45	        end
46	    end
47	
48	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
49	
50	endmodule

You are the plan reviewer. You did not write this plan. Check it against the design source, the block's contract and the correctness rules; approve it if it violates none.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_2 (precision INT19)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37]
  • output ports: result[37], chainout[37]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 37 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 37 bits (modulo 2^37), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

PLAN:

1. What is kept, what is new

The kept candidate (42 my_fir blocks) is reproduced unchanged; this revision adds the conversion of the seven fltr_compute_* modules, whose q1..q7 -> d_out_tmp stage is exactly the stage that the measurement reports as the new critical path (6 adder levels, $add~1634..1639, 7.576 ns at seed 1: a latch clock-to-Q, six 20-bit carry chains with ~1.0 ns of wire between them, 1.599 ns into $dff~1653). That stage disappears entirely.

Apply both parts to the unmodified source.

2. Part A — my_fir (reproduce the kept candidate exactly)

For each of my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h2, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4:

    f2 and h2: t0 <= (sop_s0 << 2); (4), t3 <= (sop_s3 << 8) - sop_s3; (255);
    f3: t0 <= (sop_s0 << 3) + (sop_s0 << 2); (12); h1: t0 <= (sop_s0 << 4) - sop_s0; (15); h3 and h4: t0 <= (sop_s0 << 3) + sop_s0; (9);

3. Part B — fltr_compute (new)

The seven coefficient sets are symmetric (c1=c7, c2=c6, c3=c5), so the seven products fold into four: c1*(d1+d7), c2*(d2+d6), c3*(d3+d5), c4*d4. Every product is exact in its 17-bit q register (the largest is 364*255 = 92820 < 2^17), so folding a symmetric pair into one product of the 9-bit pre-sum reproduces the pair's contribution bit for bit.

The one subtlety is the original's sign extension {q[16],q[16],q[16],q} of an unsigned product: for every i with q_i[16]=1 the 20-bit sum gets -2^17, i.e.

d_out_tmp = (sum of the seven exact products + 20'hE0000 * K) mod 2^20, K = #{ i : q_i >= 65536 },

and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3], so the correction may be added into a value wider than 20 bits and sliced at [18:3]. Only three coefficient sets can reach bit 16: f1 (277*d4, K = [d4 >= 237]), h4 (324*d4, K = [d4 >= 203]), f3 (364*d3 and 364*d5, K = [d3 >= 181] + [d5 >= 181]). For f2, h1, h2, h3 the largest product is 255*255 = 65025 < 65536, so K = 0 and no correction exists. Where a correction is needed it costs no adder: the soft term is below 2^17, so 20'hE0000*K mod 2^20 is just the three top bits of that 20-bit term (K=0 -> 3'b000, K=1 -> 3'b111, K=2 -> 3'b110).

Two products go on the block; the one or two cheap-coefficient products stay soft as shift-adds, split over the two register stages so that no stage holds more than two adder levels.

Replace each module body as follows (common head in every one of the seven):

verilog
    wire[7:0] d1 = din[55:48];  wire[7:0] d2 = din[47:40];  wire[7:0] d3 = din[39:32];
    wire[7:0] d4 = din[31:24];  wire[7:0] d5 = din[23:16];  wire[7:0] d6 = din[15:8];
    wire[7:0] d7 = din[7:0];
    wire[8:0] pa = d1 + d7;     wire[8:0] pb = d2 + d6;     wire[8:0] pc = d3 + d5;
    wire[36:0] sop_result;

and delete q1..q7 and d_out_tmp (nothing outside the module reads them; dout stays a 16-bit register).

fltr_compute_f1 (29,101,17,277) — block: 101*pb + 277*d4; soft: 29*pa + 17*pc + correction.

        .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd101), .bx({10'b0, d4}), .by(19'd277),
        .chainin(37'b0), .result(sop_result), .chainout());

    wire[16:0] tlow = ((u17 << 5) + v) - (u17 + (u17 << 1));	// 29*pa + 17*pc, <= 23460
    wire[19:0] w = sop_result[19:0] + t;

verilog

Note for the editor: every shift-add is written against a 17-bit wire (u17, pc17, s17) so no shift truncates; keep those widenings.

4. Every candidate, converted or left
  • my_fir_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (42 instances, 7 modules). Converted, as in the kept candidate: the COEF1 pair and the COEF2 pair of each filter (4 of the 6 or 7 products of each sum — the ids listed in REGIONS). Left in each: the COEF0/COEF6 pair and, where present, the COEF3 product — they stay soft because the block holds only two products and one block per my_fir instance is already a whole DSP tile; these coefficients (4, 9, 12, 15, 29, 235, 255) are one- to three-term shift-adds, cheaper than a second tile.
  • fltr_compute_f1 (lines 859-865) and fltr_compute_h4 (1065-1071). Converted: the c2 pair (860/864, 890-style 1066/1070) and the centre product (862, 1068). Left: the c1 pair (859/865, 1065/1071) and the c3 pair (861/863, 1067/1069) — their coefficients (29 and 17; 14 and 80) are one- and two-term shift-adds, so a second block (a whole tile per instance, 6 tiles per module) would cost more area than the ~35 soft BLEs they take; split over two register stages they add no more than two adder levels to any stage.
  • fltr_compute_f2 (889-895) and fltr_compute_h2 (992-998). Converted: the c2 pair (890/894, 993/997) and the c3 pair (891/893, 994/996). Left: the c1 pair (889/895, 992/998) and the centre (892, 995) — coefficient 4 is a shift and 255 is one subtract.
  • fltr_compute_f3 (928-934). Converted: the c2 pair (929/933) and the c3 pair (930/932). Left: the c1 pair (928/934), coefficient 20 = one add. (q4 is din*0 and is not a candidate.)
  • fltr_compute_h1 (959-965). Converted: 960/964 (25) and 961/963 (193). Left: 959/965, coefficient 17 = one add.
  • fltr_compute_h3 (1030-1036). Converted: 1030/1036 (23) and 1032/1034 (147). Left: 1031/1035, coefficient 72 = one add.

No candidate is left for a correctness reason; every left product is left because its coefficient is cheaper as a shift-add than a second DSP tile.

5. Blocks, tiles, and the stages
  • Blocks added: 84 — one per my_fir instance (42) and one per fltr_compute instance (42). No block is chained: every chainin is 37'b0, every chainout is unconnected, so the longest series of blocks in any stage is one block, 2.219 ns (0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019), well under the slowest stage.
  • DSP tiles after the rewrite: 84 (down from 99 in the kept candidate and 224 in the baseline). The 57 tiles that now hold the fltr_compute 9x9 products disappear: every remaining fltr multiply is an explicit shift-add. DSP area 84 x 253779 = 2.13e7, i.e. 3.8e6 below the kept candidate's, with the soft logic removed on top of that (per fltr_compute instance: seven 17-bit q registers and six 20-bit adder levels out, three 9-bit pre-adders, ~30 pipeline flip-flops, at most two shift-add levels and one 20-bit final adder in).
  • Soft logic leaving the slowest stage. The stage that leaves is exactly the measured critical stage: in each fltr_compute instance the 119 q flip-flops and the six-level 20-bit adder chain into d_out_tmp (7.576 ns at seed 1) are gone. What replaces them, per instance, is three stages of at most two adder levels each: (a) buff_out registers -> 9-bit pre-add -> block input register / stage-1 register (f1, h4: pre-add plus one shift-add level), about 0.06 + 1.0 + 1.07 + 1.6 = 3.8 ns at worst and 2.3 ns on the path into the block; (b) stage-1 registers -> at most two shift-add levels -> t, about 3.9 ns, running in parallel with the block's own 2.219 ns; (c) block result register -> one 20-bit add -> dout, about 0.06 + 0.96 + 1.07 + 1.6 = 3.7 ns. None of these is the slowest stage.
  • The slowest stage left is no longer in fltr_compute. The deepest remaining register-to-register stages are three-level soft chains elsewhere: my_fir's t3 <= (s3<<8)-(s3<<4)-(s3<<2)-s3 (three 26-bit levels) and steer_fltr's im_p_tmp/im_n_tmp (four 31-bit terms, three levels, lines 641 and 643). At the measured per-level cost of the seed-1 report (~1.07 ns a level plus ~1.6 ns into the endpoint register) that is about 5.0-5.3 ns, which is what STAGE_NS states. Both are untouched by this rewrite and neither is made slower by it.
6. Register stages, before and after
  • my_fir (unchanged from the kept candidate). Before: taps registered in the enabled delay chain, then one register (dout) over the whole products-and-sum, so operand to result was 1 stage with the multiply and six adder levels inside it. After: 2 stages (block input register, block result register), fed one cycle early from the same next-value expressions that drive the delay registers, so dout is produced on the cycle it was before; the soft t0/t3 terms take the matching single register stage and are added combinationally into dout.
  • fltr_compute (new). Before: 3 stages from din to dout — q1..q7 at edge k, d_out_tmp at edge k+1 (the six adder levels in between), dout at edge k+2. After: the same 3 stages — the block's input register at edge k (operands are the combinational pre-sums of din), the block's result register at edge k+1 (the two products and their sum in between, inside the block), dout at edge k+2 (one 20-bit add of result[19:0] and the soft term outside). The soft terms use the same two edges: a stage-1 register at edge k (u, v, s, and the comparison bits b1/b3/b5) and t at edge k+1. Operands applied before edge k therefore reach dout at edge k+2 exactly as in the original, cycle for cycle, and X-convergence after power-up is the same depth on both sides.
  • Reset: reset on every block is tied to 1'b0, as in the kept candidate. The design's reset (line 203, active low) touches only the video state machine; no register in fltr_compute or my_fir has a reset in the original, so tying the block's synchronous clear off keeps behaviour after every reset, not only at start-up. No rewrite register is relied on for an initial value.

No assumption about the design's inputs is needed: the rewrite is bit-exact for every input, including the original's sign extension of the unsigned 17-bit products, which is reproduced by the 20'hE0000 * K term in f1, f3 and h4 and is provably zero in f2, h1, h2 and h3.

DESIGN_CHANGE: in fltr_compute_* the seven products are unsigned but are summed as {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}, which subtracts 2^17 from the sum whenever a product reaches 65536 (only 277*d4, 324*d4 and 364*d3/d5 can). Widening q to 20 bits and zero-extending instead — or declaring the coefficients and q signed, which is what the commented-out negative coefficients suggest was meant — would remove the three comparators and the correction bits and let the sum go onto the block with nothing but the pre-adders outside it.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_2.v) are in sim_reference/.

The symmetry c1=c7, c2=c6, c3=c5 holds in all seven, so folding a pair into one product of the 9‑bit pre‑sum is exact (each q is 17 bits and the largest product, 364·255=92820, does not truncate).
  • The sign-extension term. {q[16],q[16],q[16],q} on unsigned products (lines 867/897/936/967/1000/1038/1073) does add 20'hE0000 per product that reaches 2^16; the plan's K is right (f1 d4≥237, h4 d4≥203, f3 d3/d5≥181; zero elsewhere, since 193·255, 147·255 and 255·255 are all < 65536), and {b,b,b,tlow} with tlow<2^17 reproduces K=0/1/2 as 000/111/110. w[18:3] of a 20-bit wrap matches d_out_tmp[18:3].
  • Soft shift-adds. 29·pa+17·pc, 4·pa+255·d4, 20·pa, 17·pa, 72·pb (with u<=pb), 14·pa+80·pc all evaluate correctly, and every intermediate fits the stated 17-bit widths with no shift truncation and no borrow.
  • Timing. fltr_compute is 3 register stages before (q, d_out_tmp, dout) and 3 after (block input reg / u,v,b at edge k; block result / t at edge k+1; dout at edge k+2), so dout is produced on the same cycle. X-convergence depth is equal; dropping the din[31:24]*0 term in f3/h1/h3 cannot make the DUT defined where the reference is X, because the fifo chain (lines 1094‑1157, 3-deep shift registers on a common wen) makes d4 X only when d5 is also X, and d5 is used.
  • Reset. Line 203's reset is active low and clears only video_state, tm3_sram_adsp, horiz, vert; neither fltr_compute nor my_fir has any reset, so reset(1'b0) on every block holds after mid-run resets, not only at start-up.
  • Visibility and terms. q1..q7 and d_out_tmp are read only inside their module; dout keeps its 16-bit register. All four product ports are used, mode_sigs/chainin tied to 0, chainout unconnected.
  • my_fir part. Faithful to the kept candidate (COEF suffixes b,c,d,1,2,3,4 and the t3 terms in f1/f2/h2 match the source); the shifted-tap operands equal r1+r5 and r2+r4 of the next cycle, and the gating at h_fltr lines 525‑553 by my_fir_rdy keeps the recomputed dout invisible on cycles where the original holds.
  • Required items. All candidates accounted for (54 converted ids, the rest left with the shift-add reason), BLOCKS 84 / TILES 84 consistent with 42+42 and the removal of all 57 fltr tiles, longest block series one block at 2.219 ns against a 5.3 ns stage, the departing soft logic named as the measured critical stage, and before/after register stages given for both regions.

1	// int_sop_2: result = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin, unsigned, modulo 2^37 (the sum wraps at the
2	// result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37] in; result[37],
4	// chainout[37] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (ax, ay, bx, by and chainin alike); the products
7	// and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (operands and
10	// chainin to chainout 1).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_2 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [17:0] ax, input [18:0] ay,
21	    input [17:0] bx, input [18:0] by,
22	    input [36:0] chainin,
23	    output reg [36:0] result,
24	    output [36:0] chainout
25	);
26	
27	    // stage 1: the input registers
28	    reg [17:0] ax_reg, bx_reg;
29	    reg [18:0] ay_reg, by_reg;
30	    reg [36:0] chainin_reg;
31	
32	    // combinational middle: the two products and their sum, from the registers
33	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 18x19 -> 37, exact
34	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
35	    wire [36:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + chainin_reg;          // modulo 2^37
36	
37	    always @(posedge clk) begin
38	        if (reset) begin
39	            result <= 0;
40	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
41	        end
42	        else begin
43	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by; chainin_reg <= chainin;
44	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
45	        end
46	    end
47	
48	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
49	
50	endmodule

  • output ports: result[37], chainout[37]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 37 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 37 bits (modulo 2^37), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
How to work
  • After each edit, run bash check.sh stereovision2.v and read its output. If it fails, fix the RTL and run it again.
  • check.sh reads the architecture's declaration of every hard block. Instantiate the block by its name and do not declare it in the design: a design that defines a module of the block's name fails the check.
  • Do not run place-and-route or any VTR command; that is done after you finish.
  • Stop when check.sh passes and its cell census shows the block instances the plan calls for.
Output
  • State what you changed, region by region, and stop.
  • Your edit is checked automatically and no person reads this, so do not end with a question or an offer.

PLAN:

1. What is kept, what is new

The kept candidate (42 my_fir blocks) is reproduced unchanged; this revision adds the conversion of the seven fltr_compute_* modules, whose q1..q7 -> d_out_tmp stage is exactly the stage that the measurement reports as the new critical path (6 adder levels, $add~1634..1639, 7.576 ns at seed 1: a latch clock-to-Q, six 20-bit carry chains with ~1.0 ns of wire between them, 1.599 ns into $dff~1653). That stage disappears entirely.

Apply both parts to the unmodified source.

2. Part A — my_fir (reproduce the kept candidate exactly)

For each of my_fir_f1, my_fir_f2, my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h2, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4:

  • make dout a wire (delete reg[28 - 1:0] dout;);
  • add, before the always block:
verilog
	wire[16:0] sop_pa = (new_data_rdy ? din : n_delay_reg1) + (new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg5);
	wire[16:0] sop_pb = (new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg1 : n_delay_reg2) + (new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg3 : n_delay_reg4);
	wire[18:0] sop_ca = `COEF1_x;		// x = b,c,d,1,2,3,4 for f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4
	wire[18:0] sop_cb = `COEF2_x;
	wire[36:0] sop_result;

	int_sop_2 sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
		.ax({1'b0, sop_pa}), .ay(sop_ca), .bx({1'b0, sop_pb}), .by(sop_cb),
		.chainin(37'b0), .result(sop_result), .chainout());

	wire[23:0] sop_s0 = din + n_delay_reg6;
	wire[25:0] sop_s3 = n_delay_reg3;	// only in f1, f2, h2
	reg[23:0] t0;
	reg[25:0] t3;				// only in f1, f2, h2
  • inside the always block, before the if (new_data_rdy ...) (i.e. unconditionally): t0 <= ...; and, where the filter has a COEF3 term, t3 <= ...; with
    f1: t0 <= (sop_s0 << 5) - (sop_s0 << 1) - sop_s0; (29), t3 <= (sop_s3 << 8) - (sop_s3 << 4) - (sop_s3 << 2) - sop_s3; (235);
    f2 and h2: t0 <= (sop_s0 << 2); (4), t3 <= (sop_s3 << 8) - sop_s3; (255);
    f3: t0 <= (sop_s0 << 3) + (sop_s0 << 2); (12); h1: t0 <= (sop_s0 << 4) - sop_s0; (15); h3 and h4: t0 <= (sop_s0 << 3) + sop_s0; (9);
  • delete the dout <= ... sum from the if branch, keeping the delay registers and output_data_ready as they are;
  • after the always block: assign dout = sop_result[27:0] + t0 + t3; (f1, f2, h2) or assign dout = sop_result[27:0] + t0; (f3, h1, h3, h4).
3. Part B — fltr_compute (new)

The seven coefficient sets are symmetric (c1=c7, c2=c6, c3=c5), so the seven products fold into four: c1*(d1+d7), c2*(d2+d6), c3*(d3+d5), c4*d4. Every product is exact in its 17-bit q register (the largest is 364*255 = 92820 < 2^17), so folding a symmetric pair into one product of the 9-bit pre-sum reproduces the pair's contribution bit for bit.

The one subtlety is the original's sign extension {q[16],q[16],q[16],q} of an unsigned product: for every i with q_i[16]=1 the 20-bit sum gets -2^17, i.e.

d_out_tmp = (sum of the seven exact products + 20'hE0000 * K) mod 2^20, K = #{ i : q_i >= 65536 },

and dout = d_out_tmp[18:3], so the correction may be added into a value wider than 20 bits and sliced at [18:3]. Only three coefficient sets can reach bit 16: f1 (277*d4, K = [d4 >= 237]), h4 (324*d4, K = [d4 >= 203]), f3 (364*d3 and 364*d5, K = [d3 >= 181] + [d5 >= 181]). For f2, h1, h2, h3 the largest product is 255*255 = 65025 < 65536, so K = 0 and no correction exists. Where a correction is needed it costs no adder: the soft term is below 2^17, so 20'hE0000*K mod 2^20 is just the three top bits of that 20-bit term (K=0 -> 3'b000, K=1 -> 3'b111, K=2 -> 3'b110).

Two products go on the block; the one or two cheap-coefficient products stay soft as shift-adds, split over the two register stages so that no stage holds more than two adder levels.

Replace each module body as follows (common head in every one of the seven):

verilog
    wire[7:0] d1 = din[55:48];  wire[7:0] d2 = din[47:40];  wire[7:0] d3 = din[39:32];
    wire[7:0] d4 = din[31:24];  wire[7:0] d5 = din[23:16];  wire[7:0] d6 = din[15:8];
    wire[7:0] d7 = din[7:0];
    wire[8:0] pa = d1 + d7;     wire[8:0] pb = d2 + d6;     wire[8:0] pc = d3 + d5;
    wire[36:0] sop_result;

and delete q1..q7 and d_out_tmp (nothing outside the module reads them; dout stays a 16-bit register).

fltr_compute_f1 (29,101,17,277) — block: 101*pb + 277*d4; soft: 29*pa + 17*pc + correction.

verilog
    int_sop_2 sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
        .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd101), .bx({10'b0, d4}), .by(19'd277),
        .chainin(37'b0), .result(sop_result), .chainout());
    reg b1; reg[8:0] u; reg[16:0] v; reg[19:0] t;
    wire[16:0] u17 = u;  wire[16:0] pc17 = pc;
    wire[16:0] tlow = ((u17 << 5) + v) - (u17 + (u17 << 1));	// 29*pa + 17*pc, <= 23460
    wire[19:0] w = sop_result[19:0] + t;
    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        u  <= pa;
        v  <= (pc17 << 4) + pc17;		// 17*pc
        b1 <= (d4 >= 8'd237);			// q4 = 277*d4 reaches bit 16
        t  <= {b1, b1, b1, tlow};
        dout <= w[18:3];
    end

fltr_compute_f2 and fltr_compute_h2 (4,42,163,255) — block: 42*pb + 163*pc; soft: 4*pa + 255*d4; K = 0.

verilog
    int_sop_2 sop (... .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd42), .bx({9'b0, pc}), .by(19'd163) ...);
    reg[8:0] u; reg[7:0] s; reg[16:0] t;
    wire[16:0] u17 = u;  wire[16:0] s17 = s;
    wire[19:0] w = sop_result[19:0] + {3'b0, t};
    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        u <= pa;  s <= d4;
        t <= (u17 << 2) + ((s17 << 8) - s17);	// 4*pa + 255*d4, <= 67065
        dout <= w[18:3];
    end

fltr_compute_f3 (20,179,364,0) — block: 179*pb + 364*pc; soft: 20*pa, plus the two-term correction in the top three bits.

verilog
    int_sop_2 sop (... .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd179), .bx({9'b0, pc}), .by(19'd364) ...);
    reg[8:0] u; reg b3, b5; reg[19:0] t;
    wire[16:0] u17 = u;
    wire[16:0] tlow = (u17 << 4) + (u17 << 2);	// 20*pa, <= 10200
    wire[19:0] w = sop_result[19:0] + t;
    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        u  <= pa;
        b3 <= (d3 >= 8'd181);  b5 <= (d5 >= 8'd181);	// q3, q5 = 364*d reach bit 16
        t  <= {(b3 | b5), (b3 | b5), (b3 ^ b5), tlow};
        dout <= w[18:3];
    end

fltr_compute_h1 (17,25,193,0) — block: 25*pb + 193*pc; soft: 17*pa; K = 0.

verilog
    int_sop_2 sop (... .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd25), .bx({9'b0, pc}), .by(19'd193) ...);
    reg[8:0] u; reg[16:0] t;  wire[16:0] u17 = u;
    wire[19:0] w = sop_result[19:0] + {3'b0, t};
    always @(posedge clk) begin u <= pa; t <= (u17 << 4) + u17; dout <= w[18:3]; end

fltr_compute_h3 (23,72,147,0) — block: 23*pa + 147*pc; soft: 72*pb; K = 0.

verilog
    int_sop_2 sop (... .ax({9'b0, pa}), .ay(19'd23), .bx({9'b0, pc}), .by(19'd147) ...);
    reg[8:0] u; reg[16:0] t;  wire[16:0] u17 = u;
    wire[19:0] w = sop_result[19:0] + {3'b0, t};
    always @(posedge clk) begin u <= pb; t <= (u17 << 6) + (u17 << 3); dout <= w[18:3]; end

fltr_compute_h4 (14,43,80,324) — block: 43*pb + 324*d4; soft: 14*pa + 80*pc + correction.

verilog
    int_sop_2 sop (... .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd43), .bx({10'b0, d4}), .by(19'd324) ...);
    reg b1; reg[8:0] u; reg[16:0] v; reg[19:0] t;
    wire[16:0] u17 = u;  wire[16:0] pc17 = pc;
    wire[16:0] tlow = ((u17 << 3) + (u17 << 2)) + ((u17 << 1) + v);	// 14*pa + 80*pc, <= 47940
    wire[19:0] w = sop_result[19:0] + t;
    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        u  <= pa;
        v  <= (pc17 << 6) + (pc17 << 4);	// 80*pc
        b1 <= (d4 >= 8'd203);			// q4 = 324*d4 reaches bit 16
        t  <= {b1, b1, b1, tlow};
        dout <= w[18:3];
    end

Note for the editor: every shift-add is written against a 17-bit wire (u17, pc17, s17) so no shift truncates; keep those widenings.

4. Every candidate, converted or left
  • my_fir_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (42 instances, 7 modules). Converted, as in the kept candidate: the COEF1 pair and the COEF2 pair of each filter (4 of the 6 or 7 products of each sum — the ids listed in REGIONS). Left in each: the COEF0/COEF6 pair and, where present, the COEF3 product — they stay soft because the block holds only two products and one block per my_fir instance is already a whole DSP tile; these coefficients (4, 9, 12, 15, 29, 235, 255) are one- to three-term shift-adds, cheaper than a second tile.
  • fltr_compute_f1 (lines 859-865) and fltr_compute_h4 (1065-1071). Converted: the c2 pair (860/864, 890-style 1066/1070) and the centre product (862, 1068). Left: the c1 pair (859/865, 1065/1071) and the c3 pair (861/863, 1067/1069) — their coefficients (29 and 17; 14 and 80) are one- and two-term shift-adds, so a second block (a whole tile per instance, 6 tiles per module) would cost more area than the ~35 soft BLEs they take; split over two register stages they add no more than two adder levels to any stage.
  • fltr_compute_f2 (889-895) and fltr_compute_h2 (992-998). Converted: the c2 pair (890/894, 993/997) and the c3 pair (891/893, 994/996). Left: the c1 pair (889/895, 992/998) and the centre (892, 995) — coefficient 4 is a shift and 255 is one subtract.
  • fltr_compute_f3 (928-934). Converted: the c2 pair (929/933) and the c3 pair (930/932). Left: the c1 pair (928/934), coefficient 20 = one add. (q4 is din*0 and is not a candidate.)
  • fltr_compute_h1 (959-965). Converted: 960/964 (25) and 961/963 (193). Left: 959/965, coefficient 17 = one add.
  • fltr_compute_h3 (1030-1036). Converted: 1030/1036 (23) and 1032/1034 (147). Left: 1031/1035, coefficient 72 = one add.

No candidate is left for a correctness reason; every left product is left because its coefficient is cheaper as a shift-add than a second DSP tile.

5. Blocks, tiles, and the stages
  • Blocks added: 84 — one per my_fir instance (42) and one per fltr_compute instance (42). No block is chained: every chainin is 37'b0, every chainout is unconnected, so the longest series of blocks in any stage is one block, 2.219 ns (0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019), well under the slowest stage.
  • DSP tiles after the rewrite: 84 (down from 99 in the kept candidate and 224 in the baseline). The 57 tiles that now hold the fltr_compute 9x9 products disappear: every remaining fltr multiply is an explicit shift-add. DSP area 84 x 253779 = 2.13e7, i.e. 3.8e6 below the kept candidate's, with the soft logic removed on top of that (per fltr_compute instance: seven 17-bit q registers and six 20-bit adder levels out, three 9-bit pre-adders, ~30 pipeline flip-flops, at most two shift-add levels and one 20-bit final adder in).
  • Soft logic leaving the slowest stage. The stage that leaves is exactly the measured critical stage: in each fltr_compute instance the 119 q flip-flops and the six-level 20-bit adder chain into d_out_tmp (7.576 ns at seed 1) are gone. What replaces them, per instance, is three stages of at most two adder levels each: (a) buff_out registers -> 9-bit pre-add -> block input register / stage-1 register (f1, h4: pre-add plus one shift-add level), about 0.06 + 1.0 + 1.07 + 1.6 = 3.8 ns at worst and 2.3 ns on the path into the block; (b) stage-1 registers -> at most two shift-add levels -> t, about 3.9 ns, running in parallel with the block's own 2.219 ns; (c) block result register -> one 20-bit add -> dout, about 0.06 + 0.96 + 1.07 + 1.6 = 3.7 ns. None of these is the slowest stage.
  • The slowest stage left is no longer in fltr_compute. The deepest remaining register-to-register stages are three-level soft chains elsewhere: my_fir's t3 <= (s3<<8)-(s3<<4)-(s3<<2)-s3 (three 26-bit levels) and steer_fltr's im_p_tmp/im_n_tmp (four 31-bit terms, three levels, lines 641 and 643). At the measured per-level cost of the seed-1 report (~1.07 ns a level plus ~1.6 ns into the endpoint register) that is about 5.0-5.3 ns, which is what STAGE_NS states. Both are untouched by this rewrite and neither is made slower by it.
6. Register stages, before and after
  • my_fir (unchanged from the kept candidate). Before: taps registered in the enabled delay chain, then one register (dout) over the whole products-and-sum, so operand to result was 1 stage with the multiply and six adder levels inside it. After: 2 stages (block input register, block result register), fed one cycle early from the same next-value expressions that drive the delay registers, so dout is produced on the cycle it was before; the soft t0/t3 terms take the matching single register stage and are added combinationally into dout.
  • fltr_compute (new). Before: 3 stages from din to dout — q1..q7 at edge k, d_out_tmp at edge k+1 (the six adder levels in between), dout at edge k+2. After: the same 3 stages — the block's input register at edge k (operands are the combinational pre-sums of din), the block's result register at edge k+1 (the two products and their sum in between, inside the block), dout at edge k+2 (one 20-bit add of result[19:0] and the soft term outside). The soft terms use the same two edges: a stage-1 register at edge k (u, v, s, and the comparison bits b1/b3/b5) and t at edge k+1. Operands applied before edge k therefore reach dout at edge k+2 exactly as in the original, cycle for cycle, and X-convergence after power-up is the same depth on both sides.
  • Reset: reset on every block is tied to 1'b0, as in the kept candidate. The design's reset (line 203, active low) touches only the video state machine; no register in fltr_compute or my_fir has a reset in the original, so tying the block's synchronous clear off keeps behaviour after every reset, not only at start-up. No rewrite register is relied on for an initial value.

No assumption about the design's inputs is needed: the rewrite is bit-exact for every input, including the original's sign extension of the unsigned 17-bit products, which is reproduced by the 20'hE0000 * K term in f1, f3 and h4 and is provably zero in f2, h1, h2 and h3.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_2.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

What changed
Part A — my_fir_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (7 modules, 6 instances each → 42 blocks)

In each module, identically:

  • dout changed from reg[27:0] to a wire (the reg[28 - 1:0] dout; declaration deleted); the dout <= (din*COEF0) + … ; statement deleted from the new_data_rdy branch. The delay chain and output_data_ready are untouched.
  • Added the next-state tap pre-sums sop_pa = (nd?din:r1)+(nd?r4:r5) and sop_pb = (nd?r1:r2)+(nd?r3:r4), feeding one int_sop_2 per instance: ax={1'b0,sop_pa}, ay=COEF1, bx={1'b0,sop_pb}, by=COEF2, chainin=37'b0, mode_sigs=12'b0, reset=1'b0, chainout() unconnected. This covers the four regions of each module (r1*C1, r2*C2, r4*C4, r5*C5), since C1=C5 and C2=C4.
  • The remaining terms register unconditionally one cycle later than before: t0 = COEF0*(din+r6) as a shift-add (29, 4, 12, 15, 4, 9, 9), and t3 = COEF3*r3 (235 in f1, 255 in f2/h2; f3/h1/h3/h4 have COEF3=0, so no t3).
  • assign dout = sop_result[27:0] + t0 [+ t3];

Feeding the block the next tap values makes sop_result after edge k equal the products of the taps as they stood just before edge k, which is what the original dout register held; h_fltr samples dout only when output_data_ready is high, so the loss of the original's enable on dout is not observable.

Part B — fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (7 modules, 6 instances each → 42 blocks)

Each module body replaced: q1..q7 and d_out_tmp deleted, dout still a 16-bit register. Common head splits din into d1..d7 and forms the symmetric pre-sums pa=d1+d7, pb=d2+d6, pc=d3+d5. One int_sop_2 per instance (same tie-offs as above):

moduleax/aybx/bysoft termsign-extension correction
f1pb/101d4/27729·pa + 17·pcb1 = d4>=237
f2, h2pb/42pc/1634·pa + 255·d4none (K=0)
f3pb/179pc/36420·pab3 = d3>=181, b5 = d5>=181
h1pb/25pc/19317·panone
h3pa/23pc/14772·pbnone
h4pb/43d4/32414·pa + 80·pcb1 = d4>=203

The original's sign extension of the unsigned 17-bit products ({q[16],q[16],q[16],q}) is reproduced as the top three bits of the 20-bit soft term t: {b1,b1,b1,tlow} for f1/h4 (K∈{0,1}) and {b3|b5, b3|b5, b3^b5, tlow} for f3 (K∈{0,1,2}, giving 000/111/110). dout <= (sop_result[19:0] + t)[18:3], with the final sum taken in 20 bits so it wraps exactly as d_out_tmp did. Register depth is unchanged at 3 stages (din→block input reg and stage-1 soft regs at edge k, block result and t at k+1, dout at k+2). Every shift-add is written against 17-bit wires so nothing truncates; all intermediate values were checked to fit.

No ASSUMES: line is needed — the rewrite is bit-exact for all inputs.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true
