PLAN:

This revision keeps the structure of the kept candidate (84 blocks, 84 tiles, same register placement) and changes three things, all of which remove soft adder bits and routed block-output nets without lengthening any stage:

  1. my_fir_f1: the block now carries COEF1=101 and COEF3=235 instead of COEF1=101 and COEF2=15. 235*n_delay_reg3 cost three soft adders of 26 bits; 15*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4) costs one soft adder of 21 bits. Net: two wide soft adders removed per instance (6 instances), and the residue path shortens from three adder levels to two.
  2. my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2: the two residues (4*(din+n_delay_reg6) and 255*n_delay_reg3) are summed into one register t03 instead of two registers t0,t3, so the path out of the block's result register passes one soft adder instead of two. The stage that builds t03 is two adder levels deep (din+n_delay_reg6 and (s3<<8)-s3 at level 1, their sum at level 2), well under the slowest stage.
  3. All 84 instances: every residue register, the final sum and the slice taken off result are narrowed to their proven maxima (all operands are unsigned, all coefficients positive), which both shrinks the soft adders and removes 3-4 routed nets per block output.

Blocks and tiles. The rewrite instantiates 84 blocks, one per my_fir instance (42) and one per fltr_compute instance (42). Each block in this mode takes a DSP tile alone and no other multiply is left in the design, so the design uses 84 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline.

Longest series of blocks in any stage. One. No block drives another: every chainin is tied to 37'b0 and every chainout is left unconnected, so no stage contains two blocks in series. The block's own stage is input register clock-to-Q + delay + output register setup = 2.219 ns, far below the slowest stage. The stages the rewrite creates and their worst case: register -> mux -> block input register = 0.060 + 1.419 + ~0.2 + 0.019 ~= 1.7 ns; block result register -> one or two soft adder levels -> capturing flop = 0.060 + 0.960 + 1.069 (+1.069 for my_fir_f1 only) + 2.25 ~= 4.3 to 5.4 ns worst case, 2 levels only in my_fir_f1 and in the fltr_compute dout path (one 20-bit add); register -> soft residue -> residue register = 0.060 + 3 x 1.069 + 0.83 ~= 4.1 ns (my_fir_f1 t0, the deepest residue left). None of these is the slowest stage: the measured period of the kept candidate, 5.12258 ns at seed 1, is set by a path with no block on it (lo05926 -> $add~270 -> lNOT~1953 -> $sub~285^MIN~87^MIN~88 -> $sub~286^MIN~85^MIN~86 -> lo00612, 84% of it wire delay) in the correlation logic, which this rewrite does not touch. STAGE_NS is stated as that stage, 5.1 ns. This revision removes adder levels from two of the rewrite's own stages (my_fir_f1's residue, my_fir_f2/h2's output add) and adds none, so it should not raise the period; the expected gain is in area and wirelength.

Soft logic that leaves which stage. In every my_fir instance the seven-product, six-level adder chain of the original dout stage is gone: two of its products (three in f1, counting the shared coefficient on both taps) move into the block and only one or two shift-add residues plus one or two final adds remain. That stage was the baseline's slowest (11.6069 ns, my_fir_f1) and is no longer slowest after either the kept candidate or this revision. In every fltr_compute instance the seven 17-bit q registers and the six-level d_out_tmp chain are gone, replaced by three 9-bit pre-sums, one or two narrow residue registers and one 20-bit add; that stage was the slowest of the kept candidate's predecessor (7.5 ns at the first pass) and is not slowest now.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region.

  • my_fir_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (dout, 6 instances each): before, one stage — the operands present in cycle c-1 are multiplied and summed combinationally into the enabled flip-flop dout, which the parent reads in cycle c (lines 525-553 latch vidin_out_temp_* only when my_fir_rdy_*, i.e. exactly when the original dout was loaded). After, two stages on the block path: the block's operands are presented one cycle early, in cycle c-2, as the values the delay line will hold in cycle c-1 (that is what the new_data_rdy muxes compute: when nd is high the line shifts, when it is low it holds, so sop_pa in cycle c-2 equals n_delay_reg1+n_delay_reg5 of cycle c-1 either way), the block registers them at edge c-1 and loads result at edge c; the residues stay one stage, registered at edge c from cycle c-1 values; dout becomes a wire, combinational from result and the residues, so it carries the cycle c-1 sum in cycle c, which is what the parent latches. dout differs from the original only in cycles the parent does not latch it (when nd was low the original held its old value), so no assumption on the inputs is needed.
  • fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (d_out_tmp then dout, 6 instances each): before, three stages (q1..q7, then d_out_tmp, then dout). After, three stages still: the block's two (operands registered at the first edge, result at the second) run in parallel with two soft register stages on the residue, and the third stage is the unchanged dout register, which takes bits [18:3] of the combinational sum of result and the residue. The block's 2-cycle latency is exactly the latency of the two register stages it replaces, so dout is unchanged cycle for cycle.

Candidates converted and left.

  • Converted, my_fir: in each module the two taps that share COEF1 (n_delay_reg1, n_delay_reg5) go onto ax*ay as one product of the pre-sum, and the second block product is COEF2 on the pre-sum of n_delay_reg2 and n_delay_reg4 — except in my_fir_f1, where it is COEF3=235 on n_delay_reg3, because 235 is the most expensive coefficient of that filter to build from shifts and 15 is the cheapest.
  • Left, my_fir: the COEF0/COEF6 taps (lines 1486/1492, 1542/1548, 1602/1607, 1661/1666, 1716/1722, 1775/1780, 1833/1838) cannot go into any block: their operand includes din of the same cycle the product is needed, and the block's result is two cycles behind its operands, so no lookahead exists for din. They stay soft as COEF0*(din+n_delay_reg6), one register stage. The COEF3 centre tap is left in my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (lines 1545, 1719) because 255 costs one soft adder while the coefficients it would displace, 42 and 163, cost two and three; it does not exist in f3, h1, h3, h4 (COEF3=0, no product in the source). The COEF2/COEF4 taps are left in my_fir_f1 (lines 1488, 1490) because the block has only two product ports and 15 is the cheapest of that filter's coefficients to build from shifts.
  • Converted, fltr_compute: the two most expensive of the four distinct products of each instance, on the symmetric pre-sums pa=d1+d7, pb=d2+d6, pc=d3+d5 or on the centre tap d4.
  • Left, fltr_compute: the remaining one or two products of each instance (lines 859/865 and 861/863 in f1; 889/895 and 892 in f2; 928/934 in f3; 959/965 in h1; 992/998 and 995 in h2; 1031/1035 in h3; 1065/1071, 1067/1069 in h4), for the same reason: two product ports per block, and these coefficients are the cheapest to build from shifts (one or two soft adders each). The q4=0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) carry no term at all. Adding a second, chained block per fltr_compute instance would fit the latency budget (3 register stages, chain adds one) and would absorb the rest, but it costs a whole DSP tile, 253779, against at most about 50 soft cells saved, so it is not taken.

Sign handling kept from the kept candidate: in the original fltr_compute each q is a 17-bit reg sign-extended by three bits into a 20-bit sum, so a product that reaches bit 16 (277*d4 in f1, 364*d3 and 364*d5 in f3, 324*d4 in h4) subtracts 2^17 from the 20-bit sum. The block computes the product unsigned, so the correction is recreated in soft logic from a comparison on the 8-bit input (d4 >= 237 in f1, d3 >= 181 and d5 >= 181 in f3, d4 >= 203 in h4), registered alongside the residue and placed in bits 19:17 of the residue. No other product of any fltr_compute instance can reach bit 16 (largest is 193*255 = 49215), and no my_fir sum can reach bit 26 (largest is 673*65535 = 44105055), so the narrowings below are exact.

module fltr_compute_f1 (clk, din, dout);

    input clk;
    input[55:0] din;
    output[15:0] dout;
    reg[15:0] dout;

    wire[7:0] d1 = din[55:48];  wire[7:0] d2 = din[47:40];  wire[7:0] d3 = din[39:32];
    wire[7:0] d4 = din[31:24];  wire[7:0] d5 = din[23:16];  wire[7:0] d6 = din[15:8];
    wire[7:0] d7 = din[7:0];
    wire[8:0] pa = d1 + d7;     wire[8:0] pb = d2 + d6;     wire[8:0] pc = d3 + d5;
    wire[36:0] sop_result;

    int_sop_2 sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
        .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd101), .bx({10'b0, d4}), .by(19'd277),
        .chainin(37'b0), .result(sop_result), .chainout());

    reg b1; reg[8:0] u; reg[14:0] v; reg[19:0] t;
    wire[14:0] u15 = u;  wire[14:0] pc15 = pc;
    wire[14:0] tlow = ((u15 << 5) + v) - (u15 + (u15 << 1));	// 29*pa + 17*pc
    wire[19:0] w = {3'b0, sop_result[16:0]} + t;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        u  <= pa;
        v  <= (pc15 << 4) + pc15;		// 17*pc
        b1 <= (d4 >= 8'd237);			// q4 = 277*d4 reaches bit 16
        t  <= {b1, b1, b1, 2'b0, tlow};
        dout <= w[18:3];
    end
 endmodule

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_2.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

// int_sop_2: result = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin, unsigned, modulo 2^37 (the sum wraps at the
// result width).
// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37] in; result[37],
// chainout[37] out. mode_sigs is not read.
// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
// at the block's entry at one clock edge (ax, ay, bx, by and chainin alike); the products
// and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (operands and
// chainin to chainout 1).
// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
// X until the first clear.
module int_sop_2 (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
    input [17:0] ax, input [18:0] ay,
    input [17:0] bx, input [18:0] by,
    input [36:0] chainin,
    output reg [36:0] result,
    output [36:0] chainout
);

    // stage 1: the input registers
    reg [17:0] ax_reg, bx_reg;
    reg [18:0] ay_reg, by_reg;
    reg [36:0] chainin_reg;

    // combinational middle: the two products and their sum, from the registers
    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 18x19 -> 37, exact
    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
    wire [36:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + chainin_reg;          // modulo 2^37

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            result <= 0;
            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
        end
        else begin
            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by; chainin_reg <= chainin;
            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
        end
    end

    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers

endmodule

        for (i = 0; i < `RESET_CYCLES; i = i + 1) tick;
        set_zero; resets_off; cmp = 1;
        phase = "lead-in";
        for (i = 0; i < `LEAD_IN; i = i + 1) tick;
        impulse_probe;
`include "drive_sv2_top.vh"
        phase = "drain"; zero_cycles(`LEAD_IN); tick;
        report;
    end

module my_fir_f1 (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout);

//coefdata=29,101,-15,-235,-15,101,29;

    input clk;
    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din;
    output[28 - 1:0] dout;
	input new_data_rdy;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;

	// PAJ - the block's operands are presented one cycle early: with the delay line
	// shifting only when new_data_rdy, these muxes are the taps of the next cycle.
	wire[16:0] sop_pa = (new_data_rdy ? din : n_delay_reg1) + (new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg5);
	wire[15:0] sop_s3 = (new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg2 : n_delay_reg3);
	wire[18:0] sop_ca = `COEF1_b;
	wire[18:0] sop_cb = `COEF3_b;
	wire[36:0] sop_result;

	int_sop_2 sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
		.ax({1'b0, sop_pa}), .ay(sop_ca), .bx({2'b0, sop_s3}), .by(sop_cb),
		.chainin(37'b0), .result(sop_result), .chainout());

	wire[16:0] sop_s0 = din + n_delay_reg6;
	wire[16:0] sop_pb = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;
	reg[21:0] t0;
	reg[20:0] tb;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		t0 <= (sop_s0 << 5) - (sop_s0 << 1) - sop_s0;	// 29*(din+n_delay_reg6)
		tb <= (sop_pb << 4) - sop_pb;			// 15*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4)
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)
		begin
			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;
			n_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;

			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;
		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end

	assign dout = {2'b0, ({1'b0, sop_result[24:0]} + t0 + tb)};
endmodule

module fltr_compute_h4 (clk, din, dout);

    input clk;
    input[55:0] din;
    output[15:0] dout;
    reg[15:0] dout;

    // PAJ - the seven taps of the symmetric filter, and the pre-sums of the pairs
    // that share a coefficient; the two widest products go into the hard block.
    wire[7:0] d1 = din[55:48];  wire[7:0] d2 = din[47:40];  wire[7:0] d3 = din[39:32];
    wire[7:0] d4 = din[31:24];  wire[7:0] d5 = din[23:16];  wire[7:0] d6 = din[15:8];
    wire[7:0] d7 = din[7:0];
    wire[8:0] pa = d1 + d7;     wire[8:0] pb = d2 + d6;     wire[8:0] pc = d3 + d5;
    wire[36:0] sop_result;

    int_sop_2 sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
        .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd43), .bx({10'b0, d4}), .by(19'd324),
        .chainin(37'b0), .result(sop_result), .chainout());

    reg b1; reg[8:0] u; reg[15:0] v; reg[19:0] t;
    wire[15:0] u16 = u;  wire[15:0] pc16 = pc;
    wire[15:0] tlow = ((u16 << 3) + (u16 << 2)) + ((u16 << 1) + v);	// 14*pa + 80*pc
    wire[19:0] w = {3'b0, sop_result[16:0]} + t;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
			u  <= pa;
			v  <= (pc16 << 6) + (pc16 << 4);	// 80*pc
			b1 <= (d4 >= 8'd203);			// q4 = 324*d4 reaches bit 16
			t  <= {b1, b1, b1, 1'b0, tlow};
          dout <= w[18:3] ;
    end
 endmodule

You are the acceptance reviewer. You did not plan or write this edit. Check the edit against the approved plan, the block's contract and the correctness rules.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_2 (precision INT19)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37]
  • output ports: result[37], chainout[37]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 37 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 37 bits (modulo 2^37), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

PLAN:

This revision keeps the structure of the kept candidate (84 blocks, 84 tiles, same register placement) and changes three things, all of which remove soft adder bits and routed block-output nets without lengthening any stage:

  1. my_fir_f1: the block now carries COEF1=101 and COEF3=235 instead of COEF1=101 and COEF2=15. 235*n_delay_reg3 cost three soft adders of 26 bits; 15*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4) costs one soft adder of 21 bits. Net: two wide soft adders removed per instance (6 instances), and the residue path shortens from three adder levels to two.
  2. my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2: the two residues (4*(din+n_delay_reg6) and 255*n_delay_reg3) are summed into one register t03 instead of two registers t0,t3, so the path out of the block's result register passes one soft adder instead of two. The stage that builds t03 is two adder levels deep (din+n_delay_reg6 and (s3<<8)-s3 at level 1, their sum at level 2), well under the slowest stage.
  3. All 84 instances: every residue register, the final sum and the slice taken off result are narrowed to their proven maxima (all operands are unsigned, all coefficients positive), which both shrinks the soft adders and removes 3-4 routed nets per block output.

Blocks and tiles. The rewrite instantiates 84 blocks, one per my_fir instance (42) and one per fltr_compute instance (42). Each block in this mode takes a DSP tile alone and no other multiply is left in the design, so the design uses 84 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline.

Longest series of blocks in any stage. One. No block drives another: every chainin is tied to 37'b0 and every chainout is left unconnected, so no stage contains two blocks in series. The block's own stage is input register clock-to-Q + delay + output register setup = 2.219 ns, far below the slowest stage. The stages the rewrite creates and their worst case: register -> mux -> block input register = 0.060 + 1.419 + ~0.2 + 0.019 ~= 1.7 ns; block result register -> one or two soft adder levels -> capturing flop = 0.060 + 0.960 + 1.069 (+1.069 for my_fir_f1 only) + 2.25 ~= 4.3 to 5.4 ns worst case, 2 levels only in my_fir_f1 and in the fltr_compute dout path (one 20-bit add); register -> soft residue -> residue register = 0.060 + 3 x 1.069 + 0.83 ~= 4.1 ns (my_fir_f1 t0, the deepest residue left). None of these is the slowest stage: the measured period of the kept candidate, 5.12258 ns at seed 1, is set by a path with no block on it (lo05926 -> $add~270 -> lNOT~1953 -> $sub~285^MIN~87^MIN~88 -> $sub~286^MIN~85^MIN~86 -> lo00612, 84% of it wire delay) in the correlation logic, which this rewrite does not touch. STAGE_NS is stated as that stage, 5.1 ns. This revision removes adder levels from two of the rewrite's own stages (my_fir_f1's residue, my_fir_f2/h2's output add) and adds none, so it should not raise the period; the expected gain is in area and wirelength.

Soft logic that leaves which stage. In every my_fir instance the seven-product, six-level adder chain of the original dout stage is gone: two of its products (three in f1, counting the shared coefficient on both taps) move into the block and only one or two shift-add residues plus one or two final adds remain. That stage was the baseline's slowest (11.6069 ns, my_fir_f1) and is no longer slowest after either the kept candidate or this revision. In every fltr_compute instance the seven 17-bit q registers and the six-level d_out_tmp chain are gone, replaced by three 9-bit pre-sums, one or two narrow residue registers and one 20-bit add; that stage was the slowest of the kept candidate's predecessor (7.5 ns at the first pass) and is not slowest now.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region.

  • my_fir_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (dout, 6 instances each): before, one stage — the operands present in cycle c-1 are multiplied and summed combinationally into the enabled flip-flop dout, which the parent reads in cycle c (lines 525-553 latch vidin_out_temp_* only when my_fir_rdy_*, i.e. exactly when the original dout was loaded). After, two stages on the block path: the block's operands are presented one cycle early, in cycle c-2, as the values the delay line will hold in cycle c-1 (that is what the new_data_rdy muxes compute: when nd is high the line shifts, when it is low it holds, so sop_pa in cycle c-2 equals n_delay_reg1+n_delay_reg5 of cycle c-1 either way), the block registers them at edge c-1 and loads result at edge c; the residues stay one stage, registered at edge c from cycle c-1 values; dout becomes a wire, combinational from result and the residues, so it carries the cycle c-1 sum in cycle c, which is what the parent latches. dout differs from the original only in cycles the parent does not latch it (when nd was low the original held its old value), so no assumption on the inputs is needed.
  • fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (d_out_tmp then dout, 6 instances each): before, three stages (q1..q7, then d_out_tmp, then dout). After, three stages still: the block's two (operands registered at the first edge, result at the second) run in parallel with two soft register stages on the residue, and the third stage is the unchanged dout register, which takes bits [18:3] of the combinational sum of result and the residue. The block's 2-cycle latency is exactly the latency of the two register stages it replaces, so dout is unchanged cycle for cycle.

Candidates converted and left.

  • Converted, my_fir: in each module the two taps that share COEF1 (n_delay_reg1, n_delay_reg5) go onto ax*ay as one product of the pre-sum, and the second block product is COEF2 on the pre-sum of n_delay_reg2 and n_delay_reg4 — except in my_fir_f1, where it is COEF3=235 on n_delay_reg3, because 235 is the most expensive coefficient of that filter to build from shifts and 15 is the cheapest.
  • Left, my_fir: the COEF0/COEF6 taps (lines 1486/1492, 1542/1548, 1602/1607, 1661/1666, 1716/1722, 1775/1780, 1833/1838) cannot go into any block: their operand includes din of the same cycle the product is needed, and the block's result is two cycles behind its operands, so no lookahead exists for din. They stay soft as COEF0*(din+n_delay_reg6), one register stage. The COEF3 centre tap is left in my_fir_f2 and my_fir_h2 (lines 1545, 1719) because 255 costs one soft adder while the coefficients it would displace, 42 and 163, cost two and three; it does not exist in f3, h1, h3, h4 (COEF3=0, no product in the source). The COEF2/COEF4 taps are left in my_fir_f1 (lines 1488, 1490) because the block has only two product ports and 15 is the cheapest of that filter's coefficients to build from shifts.
  • Converted, fltr_compute: the two most expensive of the four distinct products of each instance, on the symmetric pre-sums pa=d1+d7, pb=d2+d6, pc=d3+d5 or on the centre tap d4.
  • Left, fltr_compute: the remaining one or two products of each instance (lines 859/865 and 861/863 in f1; 889/895 and 892 in f2; 928/934 in f3; 959/965 in h1; 992/998 and 995 in h2; 1031/1035 in h3; 1065/1071, 1067/1069 in h4), for the same reason: two product ports per block, and these coefficients are the cheapest to build from shifts (one or two soft adders each). The q4=0 products (lines 931, 962, 1033) carry no term at all. Adding a second, chained block per fltr_compute instance would fit the latency budget (3 register stages, chain adds one) and would absorb the rest, but it costs a whole DSP tile, 253779, against at most about 50 soft cells saved, so it is not taken.

Sign handling kept from the kept candidate: in the original fltr_compute each q is a 17-bit reg sign-extended by three bits into a 20-bit sum, so a product that reaches bit 16 (277*d4 in f1, 364*d3 and 364*d5 in f3, 324*d4 in h4) subtracts 2^17 from the 20-bit sum. The block computes the product unsigned, so the correction is recreated in soft logic from a comparison on the 8-bit input (d4 >= 237 in f1, d3 >= 181 and d5 >= 181 in f3, d4 >= 203 in h4), registered alongside the residue and placed in bits 19:17 of the residue. No other product of any fltr_compute instance can reach bit 16 (largest is 193*255 = 49215), and no my_fir sum can reach bit 26 (largest is 673*65535 = 44105055), so the narrowings below are exact.

Code to write, module by module (applied to the unmodified source).

fltr_compute_f1 (replaces lines 841-869):

verilog
module fltr_compute_f1 (clk, din, dout);

    input clk;
    input[55:0] din;
    output[15:0] dout;
    reg[15:0] dout;

    wire[7:0] d1 = din[55:48];  wire[7:0] d2 = din[47:40];  wire[7:0] d3 = din[39:32];
    wire[7:0] d4 = din[31:24];  wire[7:0] d5 = din[23:16];  wire[7:0] d6 = din[15:8];
    wire[7:0] d7 = din[7:0];
    wire[8:0] pa = d1 + d7;     wire[8:0] pb = d2 + d6;     wire[8:0] pc = d3 + d5;
    wire[36:0] sop_result;

    int_sop_2 sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
        .ax({9'b0, pb}), .ay(19'd101), .bx({10'b0, d4}), .by(19'd277),
        .chainin(37'b0), .result(sop_result), .chainout());

    reg b1; reg[8:0] u; reg[14:0] v; reg[19:0] t;
    wire[14:0] u15 = u;  wire[14:0] pc15 = pc;
    wire[14:0] tlow = ((u15 << 5) + v) - (u15 + (u15 << 1));	// 29*pa + 17*pc
    wire[19:0] w = {3'b0, sop_result[16:0]} + t;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
        u  <= pa;
        v  <= (pc15 << 4) + pc15;		// 17*pc
        b1 <= (d4 >= 8'd237);			// q4 = 277*d4 reaches bit 16
        t  <= {b1, b1, b1, 2'b0, tlow};
        dout <= w[18:3];
    end
 endmodule

(29*pa+17*pc <= 23460 and every intermediate of tlow <= 24990, both under 2^15; 101*pb+277*d4 <= 122145, under 2^17.)

my_fir_f1 (replaces lines 1453-1499). This is the module whose block content changes:

verilog
module my_fir_f1 (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout);

    input clk; 
    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din; 
    output[28 - 1:0] dout; 
	input new_data_rdy;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;

	wire[16:0] sop_pa = (new_data_rdy ? din : n_delay_reg1) + (new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg5);
	wire[15:0] sop_s3 = (new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg2 : n_delay_reg3);
	wire[18:0] sop_ca = `COEF1_b;
	wire[18:0] sop_cb = `COEF3_b;
	wire[36:0] sop_result;

	int_sop_2 sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
		.ax({1'b0, sop_pa}), .ay(sop_ca), .bx({2'b0, sop_s3}), .by(sop_cb),
		.chainin(37'b0), .result(sop_result), .chainout());

	wire[16:0] sop_s0 = din + n_delay_reg6;
	wire[16:0] sop_pb = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4;
	reg[21:0] t0;
	reg[20:0] tb;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		t0 <= (sop_s0 << 5) - (sop_s0 << 1) - sop_s0;	// 29*(din+n_delay_reg6)
		tb <= (sop_pb << 4) - sop_pb;			// 15*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4)
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)
		begin
			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;
			n_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;
		
			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;
		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end

	assign dout = {2'b0, ({1'b0, sop_result[24:0]} + t0 + tb)};

endmodule

(101*sop_pa + 235*sop_s3 <= 28638795 < 2^25; 29*s0 <= 3801030 and its largest intermediate 32*s0 = 4194240, both < 2^22; 15*pb <= 1966050 and 16*pb = 2097120, both < 2^21; the 26-bit sum <= 34405875 < 2^26.)

(largest block sums: f3 29490750, h1 28573260, h3/h4 21626550, all < 2^25; largest residues: 1572840, 1966050, 1179630 with largest intermediate 16*s0 = 2097120, all < 2^21; largest output sums 31063590, 30539310, 22806180, all < 2^25.)

In all seven my_fir modules the line reg[28 - 1:0] dout; is deleted (dout becomes a wire driven by the assign), the delay-line shift and output_data_ready assignments inside the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) / else are kept exactly as in the source, and the dout <= ... sum is deleted from inside that if.

Every block has reset tied to 1'b0, mode_sigs to 12'b0, chainin to 37'b0 and chainout unconnected, as in the kept candidate, which the reference simulation accepted: with chainin tied to a constant the block is unchained, and no design register needs a reset to be reproduced because nothing in these two module families has a reset in the original.

DESIGN_CHANGE: all seven fltr_compute modules in a filter group are fed the same din (lines 706-712, 765-771, 824-830), so the three symmetric pre-sums d1+d7, d2+d6, d3+d5 are built seven times over in each group. Hoisting them into the parent and passing pa, pb, pc, d4 instead of the 56-bit din would delete six copies of 27 adder bits per group, 36 copies in the design, and shrink the fan-in of each filter module; it is outside the rewrite's scope, so it is not done here.

--- stereovision2.v (unmodified source)
+++ stereovision2.v (edit under review)
@@ -840,63 +840,66 @@
 endmodule
 module fltr_compute_f1 (clk, din, dout);
 
-    input clk; 
-    input[55:0] din; 
-    output[15:0] dout;

Terms. Every original tap is accounted for: block products plus soft residues reproduce 29pa+101pb+17pc+277d4 (f1), 4pa+42pb+163pc+255d4 (f2/h2), 20pa+179pb+364pc (f3), 17pa+25pb+193pc (h1), 23pa+72pb+147pc (h3), 14pa+43pb+80pc+324d4 (h4), and in my_fir the full 7-tap sums including the COEF0/COEF6 and left-behind centre taps. Binary literals in the original decode to the decimals used (e.g. 9'b100010101=277, 9'b101101100=364, 9'b101000100=324).

Sign correction. The original's 17-bit q sign-extension is −2^17 per product with bit 16 set; thresholds d4≥237 (277·236=65372<2^16), d3/d5≥181 (364·180=65520), d4≥203 (324·202=65448) are exact, and the packed fields give −2^17 for one correction ({1,1,1}=917504) and −2^18 for two ({1,1,0}=786432) mod 2^20. 1	// int_sop_2: result = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin, unsigned, modulo 2^37 (the sum wraps at the
2	// result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37] in; result[37],
4	// chainout[37] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (ax, ay, bx, by and chainin alike); the products
7	// and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (operands and
10	// chainin to chainout 1).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_2 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [17:0] ax, input [18:0] ay,
21	    input [17:0] bx, input [18:0] by,
22	    input [36:0] chainin,
23	    output reg [36:0] result,
24	    output [36:0] chainout
25	);
26	
27	    // stage 1: the input registers
28	    reg [17:0] ax_reg, bx_reg;
29	    reg [18:0] ay_reg, by_reg;
30	    reg [36:0] chainin_reg;
31	
32	    // combinational middle: the two products and their sum, from the registers
33	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 18x19 -> 37, exact
34	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
35	    wire [36:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + chainin_reg;          // modulo 2^37
36	
37	    always @(posedge clk) begin
38	        if (reset) begin
39	            result <= 0;
40	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
41	        end
42	        else begin
43	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by; chainin_reg <= chainin;
44	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
45	        end
46	    end
47	
48	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
49	
50	endmodule

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_2 (precision INT19)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37]
  • output ports: result[37], chainout[37]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 37 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 37 bits (modulo 2^37), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.
The design

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (channel width 300, median of five seeds, 1 to 5) has a worst register-to-register path of 11.6069 ns on its one clock tm3_clk_v0 (I/O pads not timed) and uses 224 DSP tiles (as packed at seed 1) of the device's 306. Its used logic-block area is 9.73358e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905) and its routed wirelength is 436921, so its area x delay x wirelength product, the objective, is 4.93619e+14. Its slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report) is in my_fir_f1: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report), in my_fir_f2 (endpoint group $dffe~642, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1, one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 11.293 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • Blocks in series are separate stages. A path through chainout starts at an input register and continues, in the same stage, into what it drives.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's chainout can drive the next block's chainin directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

PLAN:

This revision keeps revision 2's block set, block count and mapping unchanged, and repairs the one thing the measured timing report blames for the 4.99 ns period: the single soft stage in my_fir_f1 that is three adder levels deep. Everything else in the kept candidate is reproduced unchanged, because the audit below shows every other stage the rewrite leaves is at most two adder levels and so already sits near the floor that 84 blocks allow.

WHY ONLY THAT ONE STAGE CHANGES

The measured seed-1 path is lo07797.Q -> $add~184 (4 carry stages) -> lNOT~1440 -> $sub~199 (15 carry stages) -> $sub~200 (3 carry stages) -> lo00210.D = 5.015 ns to the D pin. That is exactly t0 <= (sop_s0 << 5) - (sop_s0 << 1) - sop_s0 in my_fir_f1, with sop_s0 = din + n_delay_reg6: one add then two serial subtracts, three levels. Every other soft stage the kept candidate leaves is two levels or fewer:

  • my_fir f2,h2 t03 (s0 add, 255*r3 in parallel, then the sum) = 2; f3 (s0<<3)+(s0<<2) = 2; h1 (s0<<4)-s0 = 2; h3,h4 (s0<<3)+s0 = 2; every my_fir dout tree = 1 or 2.
  • fltr_compute f1 v and tlow = 2; f2,h2 t = 2; h4 v and tlow = 2; f3, h1, h3 = 1; every dout add = 1.

At the sampled rates (register clk-to-Q 0.060, register-to-logic wire ~1.0, adder cell plus wire to the next ~1.07, wire to a register 0.83) a two-level soft stage is ~3.3 ns and a three-level one ~4.4-5.0 ns, which matches the measurement. So removing the one three-level stage is the whole available delay win at this block count; no further soft restructuring lowers the period, because re-partitioning a two-level residue only moves the second level between the t stage and the dout stage (both start at a clk-to-Q and end at a setup and cost the same), and driving every soft stage to one level would require a second block in each my_fir and each fltr_compute instance.

I considered and rejected adding blocks:

  • Two chained blocks per instance: chainout costs 0.060+2.140 plus a block-to-block wire (median 1.17) plus 0.019 = ~3.4 ns for that stage, and it buys only the removal of one 20-bit add; worse, in my_fir it is impossible, because a chained first block needs its operands two cycles before the result and the tap values two cycles ahead depend on new_data_rdy of a cycle that has not happened yet.
  • Two unchained blocks per my_fir instance (all four pair-products in hardware): the dout stage still has three inputs (two results plus the registered c0*din term) and stays two levels, so the period does not move, while 42 extra tiles cost ~1.07e7 area (+21%) and more routed wire. Rejected.
  • Two unchained blocks per fltr_compute f1/h4 instance: the dout stage still has three inputs (two results plus the overflow-correction term), still two levels. Rejected.
  • Splitting the pair pre-sums across both product slots to take the 17-bit adder out of the block-input path: that needs three blocks per my_fir instance. Rejected.

THE CHANGE IN my_fir_f1 (the only difference from the kept candidate)

Keep the block, its operands and tb exactly as in the kept candidate. Replace the three-level t0 with two registers that are each at most two levels from din/n_delay_reg6, and balance the output tree:

verilog
    reg[21:0] t0;                   // 28*(din + n_delay_reg6)
    reg[16:0] t1;                   //     din + n_delay_reg6
    reg[20:0] tb;                   // 15*(n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4)
    ...
        t0 <= (sop_s0 << 5) - (sop_s0 << 2);
        t1 <= sop_s0;
        tb <= (sop_pb << 4) - sop_pb;
    ...
    assign dout = (({3'b0, sop_result[24:0]} + {7'b0, tb}) + ({6'b0, t0} + {11'b0, t1}));

t0 + t1 = 28*s0 + s0 = 29*(din + n_delay_reg6), the same term the kept candidate computes, so the value of dout is unchanged on every cycle. Widths: sop_s0 is 17 bits and the 22-bit assignment context extends it before the shifts, so 28*s0 <= 3669960 < 2^22; tb <= 1966050 < 2^21; sop_result = 101*(r1+r5) + 235*r3 <= 28650 ... < 2^25; the four 28-bit terms sum to at most 34414350 < 2^26, so the 28-bit dout never wraps, exactly as in the original. The parentheses must be written as shown: a flat a + b + c + d is left-associated by the synthesiser into three serial adders, which would reinstate a three-level stage.

Stage effect: the t0 stage becomes din/n_delay_reg6 register -> one add (sop_s0) -> one subtract -> t0 register, two levels (~3.3 ns); t1 is one level (~2.2 ns); the dout stage becomes a balanced 4-input tree, two levels (~3.3 ns), the same depth the kept candidate's 3-input dout tree already had. The 29x chain leaves the t0 stage; that stage was the slowest stage of the whole design and is no longer slowest.

  • f2, h2: reg[24:0] t03; t03 <= (sop_s0<<2) + ((sop_s3<<8) - sop_s3); assign dout = {2'b0, ({1'b0, sop_result[24:0]} + t03)};

CANDIDATES CONVERTED AND LEFT

Converted (53 ids, listed in REGIONS, 6 instances each): in every fltr_compute instance the two widest products of the 4 distinct products of its symmetric 7-tap kernel (after pairing the equal-coefficient taps) go into the block's two product slots — f1 101*(d2+d6) and 277*d4; f2/h2 42*(d2+d6) and 163*(d3+d5); f3 179*(d2+d6) and 364*(d3+d5); h1 25*(d2+d6) and 193*(d3+d5); h3 23*(d1+d7) and 147*(d3+d5); h4 43*(d2+d6) and 324*d4. In every my_fir instance the two widest pair-products go into the block — f1 101*(r1+r5) and 235*r3; f2/h2 42*(r1+r5) and 163*(r2+r4); f3 77/148; h1 25/193; h3/h4 56/109.

Left, with the reason, grouped:

  • fltr_compute_f1 859$44, 861$46, 863$48, 865$50 (29*d1, 17*d3, 17*d5, 29*d7); fltr_compute_f2 889$58, 892$61, 895$64; fltr_compute_f3 928$72, 931$75-equivalent slot (the 0-coefficient tap is not a candidate), 934$78; fltr_compute_h1 959$86, 962$89-equivalent, 965$92; fltr_compute_h2 992$100, 995$103, 998$106; fltr_compute_h3 1031$115, 1033$117, 1035$119; fltr_compute_h4 1065$128, 1067$130, 1069$132, 1071$134: the block has only two product slots and these are the cheaper coefficients (each is 1 or 2 shifted terms), so they are kept outside as the registered residue t and added to result in one adder level.
  • my_fir_f1 1486$154, 1488$157, 1490$161, 1492$165; my_fir_f2 1542$169, 1545$174, 1548$180; my_fir_f3 1602$184, 1607$193; my_fir_h1 1661$197, 1666$206; my_fir_h2 1716$210, 1719$215, 1722$221; my_fir_h3 1775$225, 1780$234; my_fir_h4 1833$238, 1838$247: same slot limit, plus a hard structural reason for the din tap. A my_fir block's operands must be presented one cycle before the delay line shifts (the block needs 2 cycles and dout must be right in the cycle output_data_ready is high), and din of that later cycle does not exist yet, so c0*din can never be a block product. It and its paired tap c0*n_delay_reg6 stay soft.
  • Everything in my_fir_f1 beyond the three converted products is left for the same reasons; in particular 15*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4) stays soft because both block slots are taken by the two widest products.

BLOCKS, TILES, AND THE LONGEST SERIES OF BLOCKS

The rewrite instantiates 84 blocks and adds none over the kept candidate: 42 fltr_compute instances x 1 + 42 my_fir instances x 1. Each block in this mode takes a DSP tile alone, and no other multiply survives synthesis in the design, so the design uses 84 DSP tiles against the baseline's 224 (the device has 306). The longest series of blocks in any stage is one: chainin is tied to 37'b0 on every block and chainout is left unconnected, so no stage contains two blocks. That one-block stage is the block's internal path, 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns, well under the slowest stage.

STAGE ACCOUNTING

Stages the rewrite leaves, with estimates from the sampled rates:

  1. my_fir tap registers -> tap mux (one LUT) -> 17-bit pre-sum adder -> block input register: 0.060 + ~1.0 + 0.15 + ~0.79 + ~0.5 + 1.419 (register-to-first-block wire) + 0.019 = ~3.9 ns. This is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves and is unchanged from the kept candidate; shortening it would require a third product slot per coefficient group, i.e. two or three extra blocks per instance, which costs far more area and wire than the ~0.5 ns it could buy.
  2. Two-level soft stages, ~3.3 ns each and not slowest: the my_fir residue registers (t0/t03), the my_fir dout trees, fltr_compute f1's v/t and h4's v/t.
  3. One-level soft stages, ~2.2-2.8 ns: fltr_compute pre-sums into the block, fltr_compute f3/h1/h3 residues, every fltr_compute dout add, my_fir t1.
  4. Block internal, 2.219 ns.

Soft logic leaving a stage, relative to the kept candidate: the second subtract of 29*(din+n_delay_reg6) leaves the my_fir_f1 t0 stage (that stage was the design's slowest at 5.015 ns and drops to two levels), at the price of one more add in the my_fir_f1 dout stage, which stays two levels and is not slowest. Relative to the baseline, six adder levels with their carry chains and the LUT in front of the enabled flip-flop leave every my_fir sum stage, and six adder levels plus the seven 17-bit product registers leave every fltr_compute sum stage; those were the baseline's two slowest stages.

REGISTER STAGES, BEFORE AND AFTER, FOR EACH CONVERTED REGION

  • fltr_compute (all 7 modules): before, 3 stages from din to dout — products into q1..q7 (1), the 7-term adder chain into d_out_tmp (2), the slice into dout (3); the candidate table's "products registered 1 stage before the sum". After, still 3 stages: operands into the block's input registers (1), the two products and their sum into the block's result (2), result + t sliced into dout (3). The soft residue runs alongside on its own two register stages (u/v/b1, then t), so it lands in the same cycle as result. Latency and every output cycle are unchanged.
  • my_fir (all 7 modules): before, 1 enabled register stage from the taps to dout ("products registered 0 stages before the sum"). After, 2 register stages inside the block, fed one cycle early: the operands presented in cycle k-1 are the tap values of cycle k (the mux on new_data_rdy predicts the shift exactly, because the delay line moves only when new_data_rdy is high), so the block's result holds the cycle-k sum during cycle k+1 — the same cycle in which the original's dout register held it. The design register dout becomes a wire; the block's two registers replace it plus one cycle of look-ahead. dout is read only by h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_*, which samples it under my_fir_rdy_* (= output_data_ready, one cycle after new_data_rdy), and output_data_ready keeps its original register, so the sampled value is unchanged on every cycle.

CORRECTNESS NOTES

Every block is driven .reset(1'b0): no register of these filters is reset in the original (the design's reset input does not reach them), so the block must never clear, and the testbench's mid-run resets leave these paths alone. No rewrite relies on a power-up value: the added registers come up unknown exactly as the originals' do, and dout is only consumed under output_data_ready / after the fltr_compute pipeline has filled. All block arithmetic is unsigned and exact: every operand is zero-extended into its port and no sum reaches 2^37. The original's per-product 17-bit truncation with sign extension into a 20-bit sum is reproduced bit-for-bit in fltr_compute f1 (b1 when 277*d4 >= 2^16, i.e. d4 >= 237), f3 (b3,b5 when 364*d >= 2^16, i.e. d >= 181) and h4 (b1 when 324*d4 >= 2^16, i.e. d4 >= 203) by adding 7*2^17 (== -2^17 mod 2^20) per overflowing product; no other product in any module reaches bit 16. In my_fir no truncation occurs in the original (16-bit taps, coefficient sum 525, 28-bit dout), so the block sums are exact. No value that leaves a module is hidden inside a block: output_data_ready, the delay line and dout all keep their original visibility, and chainout is read by nothing.

No ASSUMES: the rewrite is unconditionally equivalent, including for back-to-back new_data_rdy and for new_data_rdy low for arbitrarily long.

DESIGN_CHANGE: Two changes to the design itself, outside this rewrite, would help. (1) steer_fltr lines 640-643 compute 3- and 4-term 31-bit sums as left-associated chains (A - B + C - D), i.e. up to three serial 31-bit carry chains in one register-to-register stage; nothing there is a multiply, so no candidate covers it, and with the filters now on blocks it is a likely next limiter. Writing those as balanced trees, or giving them one more pipeline stage, would shorten it. (2) If my_fir's dout were allowed one more cycle of latency (with output_data_ready delayed to match, which changes when h_fltr samples), the c0*din tap product and the new_data_rdy prediction muxes would both disappear: the tap pre-sums could be read straight out of the delay registers, two chained blocks would cover all four pair-products, and every soft adder in my_fir would go away.

1	// int_sop_2: result = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin, unsigned, modulo 2^37 (the sum wraps at the
2	// result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37] in; result[37],
4	// chainout[37] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (ax, ay, bx, by and chainin alike); the products
7	// and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (operands and
10	// chainin to chainout 1).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_2 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [17:0] ax, input [18:0] ay,
21	    input [17:0] bx, input [18:0] by,
22	    input [36:0] chainin,
23	    output reg [36:0] result,
24	    output [36:0] chainout
25	);
26	
27	    // stage 1: the input registers
28	    reg [17:0] ax_reg, bx_reg;
29	    reg [18:0] ay_reg, by_reg;
30	    reg [36:0] chainin_reg;
31	
32	    // combinational middle: the two products and their sum, from the registers
33	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 18x19 -> 37, exact
34	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
35	    wire [36:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + chainin_reg;          // modulo 2^37
36	
37	    always @(posedge clk) begin
38	        if (reset) begin
39	            result <= 0;
40	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
41	        end
42	        else begin
43	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by; chainin_reg <= chainin;
44	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
45	        end
46	    end
47	
48	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
49	
50	endmodule

Task

You are the plan reviewer. You did not write this plan. Check it against the design source, the block's contract and the correctness rules; approve it if it violates none.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_2 (precision INT19)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37]
  • output ports: result[37], chainout[37]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 37 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 37 bits (modulo 2^37), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
