With nd=new_data_rdy the block operands are the taps of the next cycle, read one cycle early: sop_pa=(nd?din_q:n_delay_reg1)+(nd?n_delay_reg4:n_delay_reg5) [=r1+r5 of the next cycle], sop_pb_mux=(nd?n_delay_reg1:n_delay_reg2)+(nd?n_delay_reg3:n_delay_reg4) [=r2+r4], sop_s3=(nd?n_delay_reg2:n_delay_reg3) [=r3]. f1: ax={1'b0,sop_pa} ay=19'd101 bx={2'b0,sop_s3} by=19'd235; f2,h2: ax={1'b0,sop_pa} ay=19'd42 bx={1'b0,sop_pb_mux} by=19'd163; f3: ay=19'd77 by=19'd148; h1: ay=19'd25 by=19'd193; h3,h4: ay=19'd56 by=19'd109 (ax={1'b0,sop_pa}, bx={1'b0,sop_pb_mux} in those four). result[24:0] plus the registered soft residues drives dout combinationally. (B) fltr_compute, one block per instance except that f2 and h2 of the same v_fltr share one block instantiated in v_fltr; .clk(clk) .reset(1'b0) .mode_sigs(12'b0) .chainin(37'b0) .chainout(); d1..d7=din[55:48],[47:40],[39:32],[31:24],[23:16],[15:8],[7:0], pa=d1+d7, pb=d2+d6, pc=d3+d5 — f1 ax={9'b0,pb} ay=19'd101 bx={10'b0,d4} by=19'd277; f2,h2 (shared) ax={9'b0,pb} ay=19'd42 bx={9'b0,pc} by=19'd163; f3 ax={9'b0,pb} ay=19'd179 bx={9'b0,pc} by=19'd364; h1 ax={9'b0,pb} ay=19'd25 bx={9'b0,pc} by=19'd193; h3 ax={9'b0,pa} ay=19'd23 bx={9'b0,pc} by=19'd147; h4 ax={9'b0,pb} ay=19'd43 bx={10'b0,d4} by=19'd324. In every fltr_compute instance the low bits of result are added to one registered soft term t and dout is driven COMBINATIONALLY: assign dout = (result-part + t)[18:3].
PLAN:

This revision keeps the arithmetic mapping that measured 4.12291 ns / 5.20677e7 / 208981 and changes two things: (1) the pipeline register that sits between a fltr_compute and the my_fir it feeds is moved from the fltr_compute output to the my_fir input, which takes the long v_fltr-to-h_fltr wire out of the three-hop stage that is now critical and puts it in a two-hop stage that has slack; (2) the fltr_compute_f2 and fltr_compute_h2 instances of one v_fltr, which are the same seven products of the same din (lines 889-895 vs 992-998, both instantiated on {buff_out1..buff_out7} at 707/710, 766/769, 825/828), share one block instead of two, so the design uses 78 tiles instead of 84.

Why this attacks the measured path. The seed-1 report shows the whole critical stage is routing: 0.060 clock-to-Q, 1.702 wire into the new_data_rdy mux, 0.153 mux, 1.000 wire into the 17-bit pre-adder, 0.188 carry chain, 1.001 wire into int_sop_2.ax. Three cell-to-cell hops; the first of them, 1.702 ns, is the operand arriving at the mux. din of a my_fir is the dout register of a fltr_compute in another module instance (v_fltr feeds h_fltr through the top at lines 185-197), and that register's output is one of the two mux inputs of sop_pa. Moving that register across the module boundary leaves the arithmetic and the latency untouched (the register is moved, not added or removed) but relocates its long wire into the fltr_compute output stage, which after the move is block result -> one 20-bit add -> wire -> din_q (0.060 + 0.960 + 0.19 + ~1.7 + 0.019 = ~2.9 ns), while the my_fir input stage becomes a local register -> mux -> pre-adder -> block (0.060 + ~0.6 + 0.153 + ~1.0 + 0.19 + ~1.0 + 0.019 = ~3.0 ns). The same move also shortens the my_fir soft-residue stage, which starts at din too.

Step 1, the register move (all 7 fltr_compute modules and all 7 my_fir modules).

  • In each fltr_compute, dout becomes a wire: assign dout = w[18:3]; instead of dout <= w[18:3];. Everything upstream of it is unchanged, so the module keeps two register stages (block input registers and the soft u/v/b registers at stage 1; block result register and the soft t register at stage 2).
  • In each my_fir, add reg [15:0] din_q; with always @(posedge clk) din_q <= din; (unconditional, no enable, exactly like the register it replaces) and replace every read of din in the module by din_q, including n_delay_reg1 <= din_q inside the new_data_rdy branch.
  • Equivalence: in the original, fltr_compute.dout is a register whose D is the final combinational value and my_fir.din is that register's output; after the move din_q is a register with the same D and the same clock, so din_q is cycle-for-cycle the original din. The taps-to-dout latency of fltr_compute (3 edges: q, d_out_tmp, dout) is still 3 edges (block input register, block result register, din_q). No other reader exists: v_fltr's vidin_out_f1..h4 go only to h_fltr (top lines 185-197) and h_fltr uses vidin_in_f1..h4 only as the din of one my_fir each (lines 514-520), so one moved register per net is enough and nothing else sees the now-combinational output. din_q powers up unknown exactly as the register it replaces did, and flushes on the first clocked load.

Step 2, the shared f2/h2 block.

  • Delete the int_sop_2 instance from fltr_compute_f2 and from fltr_compute_h2 and give both modules an extra input input [36:0] sop_result; in place of it; the rest of those two modules (the pa/pb/pc adders, the u, s and t registers, assign dout = w[18:3]) is unchanged.
  • In each of v_fltr_496x7, v_fltr_316x7, v_fltr_226x7 add
    wire [8:0] fc2_pb = buff_out2 + buff_out6; wire [8:0] fc2_pc = buff_out3 + buff_out5; wire [36:0] fc2_sop;
    int_sop_2 sop_f2h2 (.clk(tm3_clk_v0), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0), .ax({9'b0, fc2_pb}), .ay(19'd42), .bx({9'b0, fc2_pc}), .by(19'd163), .chainin(37'b0), .result(fc2_sop), .chainout());
    and pass fc2_sop to both inst_fltr_compute_f2 and inst_fltr_compute_h2.
  • This is sound because the two instances receive the identical 56-bit din and carry identical coefficients (4,42,163,255,163,42,4), so their products, their sums and their outputs are equal on every cycle; one block's result serves both reductions. Nothing else changes: both modules keep their own soft residue and their own output.

Step 3, the per-module arithmetic (unchanged from the measured candidate; restated so the editor can apply it to the unmodified source).

my_fir (nd = new_data_rdy; taps as in the source; the block is read one cycle early because it spends two edges where the original dout register spent one, and dout is now combinational into h_fltr's enabled vidin_out_reg):

  • common wires: sop_pa, sop_pb_mux, sop_s3 as in MAPPING; sop_s0 = din_q + n_delay_reg6 (current taps, no mux, because the soft terms are registered one cycle later than the block operands).
  • f1 (29,101,15,235,15,101,29): block 101*(r1+r5) + 235*r3; soft t0 <= (sop_s0<<5)-(sop_s0<<2), t1 <= sop_s0, tb <= (sop_pb<<4)-sop_pb with sop_pb = n_delay_reg2 + n_delay_reg4; assign dout = (({3'b0,sop_result[24:0]} + {7'b0,tb}) + ({6'b0,t0} + {11'b0,t1}));
  • f2 and h2 (4,42,163,255,163,42,4): block 42*(r1+r5) + 163*(r2+r4); soft t03 <= (sop_s0<<2) + ((sop_s3_raw<<8) - sop_s3_raw) with sop_s3_raw = n_delay_reg3; assign dout = {2'b0, ({1'b0,sop_result[24:0]} + t03)};
  • f3 (12,77,148,0,148,77,12): block 77*(r1+r5) + 148*(r2+r4); soft t0 <= (sop_s0<<3)+(sop_s0<<2); assign dout = {3'b0, (sop_result[24:0] + {4'b0,t0})};
  • h1 (15,25,193,0,193,25,15): block 25*(r1+r5) + 193*(r2+r4); soft t0 <= (sop_s0<<4)-sop_s0; dout as f3.
  • h3 and h4 (9,56,109,0,109,56,9): block 56*(r1+r5) + 109*(r2+r4); soft t0 <= (sop_s0<<3)+sop_s0; dout as f3.
  • the tap shifting, output_data_ready and the new_data_rdy branch are left exactly as in the source except that din reads become din_q.

fltr_compute (three register stages become two inside the module plus din_q in my_fir; the original sign-extends each 17-bit product with its own bit 16, so the terms whose product reaches bit 16 must keep that wrap, which is what the b-registers below reproduce):

  • f1 (29,101,17,277): block 101*pb + 277*d4; u <= pa; v <= (pc<<4)+pc; b1 <= (d4 >= 8'd237); t <= {b1,b1,b1,2'b0,tlow} with tlow = ((u<<5)+v) - (u+(u<<1)) on 15 bits; w = {3'b0, sop_result[16:0]} + t; assign dout = w[18:3];
  • f2 and h2 (4,42,163,255): shared block 42*pb + 163*pc; u <= pa; s <= d4; t <= (u<<2) + ((s<<8)-s) on 17 bits; w = {3'b0, sop_result[16:0]} + {3'b0,t}; assign dout = w[18:3];
  • f3 (20,179,364,0): block 179*pb + 364*pc; u <= pa; b3 <= (d3>=8'd181); b5 <= (d5>=8'd181); t <= {(b3|b5),(b3|b5),(b3^b5),3'b0,tlow} with tlow = (u<<4)+(u<<2); w = {1'b0, sop_result[18:0]} + t; assign dout = w[18:3];
  • h1 (17,25,193,0): block 25*pb + 193*pc; u <= pa; t <= (u<<4)+u; w = {3'b0, sop_result[16:0]} + {6'b0,t}; assign dout = w[18:3];
  • h3 (23,72,147,0): block 23*pa + 147*pc; u <= pb; t <= (u<<6)+(u<<3); w = {3'b0, sop_result[16:0]} + {4'b0,t}; assign dout = w[18:3];
  • h4 (14,43,80,324): block 43*pb + 324*d4; u <= pa; v <= (pc<<6)+(pc<<4); b1 <= (d4>=8'd203); t <= {b1,b1,b1,1'b0,tlow} with tlow = ((u<<3)+(u<<2)) + ((u<<1)+v) on 16 bits; w = {3'b0, sop_result[16:0]} + t; assign dout = w[18:3];

Candidates converted and candidates left.

  • Converted (53 ids, listed in REGIONS, 6 instances each): in every my_fir the symmetric pair on taps 1 and 5 and the pair on taps 2 and 4 (f1 takes the centre tap 3 instead of the 2/4 pair, f2/h2 take the 2/4 pair and leave the centre), and in every fltr_compute two of the four coefficient groups.
  • Left, group 1 - the outer tap pair of every my_fir (1486 and 1492, 1542 and 1548, 1602 and 1607, 1661 and 1666, 1716 and 1722, 1775 and 1780, 1833 and 1838): tap 0 is the live input din. A block operand applied at edge k-1 must already carry the tap vector of edge k, which for tap 0 is next cycle's din and does not exist yet; this group therefore stays in soft logic, where it is evaluated one cycle later from the current registers (sop_s0) and added to the block result. The same argument forbids chaining a second block into any my_fir: the upstream block of a chain would need operands one further cycle early, i.e. it would need new_data_rdy of the following edge.
  • Left, group 2 - one more group per 4-group my_fir (f1 lines 1488 and 1490, the 15*(t2+t4) pair; f2/h2 lines 1545 and 1719, the 255*t3 centre tap): a block holds two products and these FIRs have four coefficient groups, one of which is already forced soft, so exactly one more must stay soft. The cheapest was chosen in each case (16x-x, and 256x-x folded into the same registered term as 4*(t0+t6)).
  • Left, group 3 - the outer tap pair of every fltr_compute (859/865, 889/895, 928/934, 959/965, 992/998, 1031/1035, 1065/1071) and, where the module has four groups, the remaining group (861/863 for f1, 892 for f2, 995 for h2, 1067/1069 for h4): two products per block, four groups per module. These stay in soft logic as one registered term each, two adder levels deep.
  • No candidate is left for lack of a correct rewrite; mode_sigs is tied to 0, chainin to 0, chainout is unconnected, and the block reset is tied low because none of the registers these rewrites replace has a reset in the source (the filter registers are written only by their always @(posedge clk) blocks, lines 856-869, 1474-1498 and their copies), so a cleared block would not match the original.

Blocks, tiles, and the longest series of blocks. The rewrite instantiates 78 blocks: one per my_fir instance (42) and one per fltr_compute instance except that f2 and h2 of a v_fltr share one (36). Each block takes a DSP tile alone and no other multiply is left in the design, so the design uses 78 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 84 in the measured candidate. No block drives another: the longest series of blocks in any stage is one, and that stage is the block-internal stage, 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns, well under the slowest stage.

Stages after the rewrite, and which soft logic leaves which stage.

  • my_fir input stage (din_q and the tap registers -> new_data_rdy mux -> 17-bit pre-adder -> block operand register): this is the stage that measured 4.12291 ns. The mux and the pre-adder stay; what leaves it is the long inter-module wire, which moves into the fltr_compute output stage. Estimate 0.060 + 0.6 + 0.153 + 1.0 + 0.19 + 1.0 + 0.019 = ~3.0 ns. It is the stage the rewrite is aimed at and is no longer expected to be the slowest.
  • fltr_compute output stage (block result -> the single 20-bit w add -> the v_fltr-to-h_fltr wire -> din_q): two hops, estimate 0.060 + 0.960 + 0.19 + 1.7 + 0.019 = ~2.9 ns. What leaves the old version of this stage is nothing; what enters it is the long wire. It absorbs the wire because the original seven-term, three-level d_out_tmp adder tree and the seven constant multiplies already left this module for the block.
  • my_fir output stage (block result -> one 25-bit add -> h_fltr's enabled vidin_out_reg) for f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4: 0.060 + 0.960 + 0.19 + ~1.0 = ~2.2 ns. For f1 the tree is two levels ((result+tb)+(t0+t1)), ~3.4 ns; this and the fltr_compute output stage are the likely new slowest stages, which is why STAGE_NS is given as 3.5 rather than 3.0. The six adder levels and the LUT of the baseline's critical stage are gone from here: all that remains is one or two adder levels.
  • my_fir soft-residue stage (din_q and the tap registers -> at most two adder levels -> t0/t1/tb/t03): ~3.3 ns, and it too gains from din_q being local. fltr_compute input stage (buff_out registers -> pa/pb/pc -> block): ~2.7 ns. Block internal: 2.219 ns.
  • Slowest stage left: ~3.5 ns, against the baseline's 11.6069 ns and the measured candidate's 4.12291 ns. Area falls by the six blocks the f2/h2 sharing removes (6 x 253779 = 1.52e6, about 2.9 percent of the measured area) with no change in what is computed; wirelength should fall with them and with the long operand nets no longer having to reach a mux and an adder before the DSP.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region.

  • my_fir (all seven modules): before, the seven products are formed combinationally from din and n_delay_reg1..6 and summed in the same stage, landing in the dout register one edge after the taps; h_fltr then samples dout into vidin_out_reg one edge later, two register stages from the taps in total. After, the converted products and their partial sum sit between the block's two registers: the operands are the muxed next-cycle taps applied one cycle early, the block's input register takes them at edge k-1, its result register at edge k, and dout, now combinational, is sampled by the unchanged enabled vidin_out_reg at edge k+1 - still two register stages from the taps, with the same value on every cycle. The soft residue keeps its single register, loaded one cycle later than the block operands from the un-muxed current taps, which is what makes the two halves line up.
  • fltr_compute (all seven modules): before, the products are registered in q1..q7 one stage before the d_out_tmp sum, and dout is a third stage. After, the converted products and their sum sit between the block's two registers (stage 1 and stage 2, alongside the soft u/v/b and t registers), and the third register is my_fir's din_q; three register stages from din to the value my_fir reads, exactly as before. The block's result register replaces d_out_tmp for the converted part; the register that used to be fltr_compute's dout is moved, not removed.

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f2 and fltr_compute_h2 are the same filter on the same input in every v_fltr, so vidin_out_f2 and vidin_out_h2 are always equal; deleting inst_fltr_compute_h2 and wiring vidin_out_h2 to vidin_out_f2 would remove six more instances' worth of soft logic on top of the six blocks this plan already shares. The same holds one level up for my_fir_f2/my_fir_h2 and my_fir_h3/my_fir_h4, which are pairs of identical filters on different inputs: making them one parameterised module would not save hardware, but giving the four-group FIRs a non-zero centre tap pattern that pairs with the outer taps would let a single block cover more of each sum.

For each my_fir the block value stays below 2²⁵ so sop_result[24:0] is exact, and t0/t1/tb/t03 carry the remaining taps with no truncation; the zero-extensions on dout match bits the original sum could never set.

Timing. The one-cycle-early read is sound: sop_pa/sop_pb_mux/sop_s3 sampled at edge k−1 under nd(k−1) equal r1+r5, r2+r4, r3 after edge k−1 in both branches, so result at edge k lines up with the soft terms registered at edge k from din_q(k−1)/n_delay_reg*(k−1).

1	// int_sop_2: result = ax*ay + bx*by + chainin, unsigned, modulo 2^37 (the sum wraps at the
2	// result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax[18], ay[19], bx[18], by[19], chainin[37] in; result[37],
4	// chainout[37] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (ax, ay, bx, by and chainin alike); the products
7	// and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (operands and
10	// chainin to chainout 1).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_2 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [17:0] ax, input [18:0] ay,
21	    input [17:0] bx, input [18:0] by,
22	    input [36:0] chainin,
23	    output reg [36:0] result,
24	    output [36:0] chainout
25	);
26	
27	    // stage 1: the input registers
28	    reg [17:0] ax_reg, bx_reg;
29	    reg [18:0] ay_reg, by_reg;
30	    reg [36:0] chainin_reg;
31	
32	    // combinational middle: the two products and their sum, from the registers
33	    wire [36:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 18x19 -> 37, exact
34	    wire [36:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
35	    wire [36:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + chainin_reg;          // modulo 2^37
36	
37	    always @(posedge clk) begin
38	        if (reset) begin
39	            result <= 0;
40	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
41	        end
42	        else begin
43	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by; chainin_reg <= chainin;
44	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
45	        end
46	    end
47	
48	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
49	
50	endmodule

layout koios_small · used area 9.73358e+07 · critical path 11.6069 ns · wirelength 436921 · area x delay x wirelength (delay register to register, 2026-10-20) 4.93619e+14 (read from entry; median per term over the entry's seed runs (its seed_medians; seeds lists them))

The objective is area x delay x wirelength (delay register to register, 2026-10-20): VPR's total used logic block area (I/Os and empty grid tiles excluded) times the critical path times the total routed wirelength. Each term is the median over the loop's seeds; the product is the product of the medians. Beside every product stand the ratios against the baseline, A/A0 (area), D/D0 (critical path), W/W0 (wirelength) and their product, so the normalization can be read off. After each measured rewrite, the planner is given every measurement so far and asked for a revision. A revision is built and checked like the first rewrite, and the lowest product is kept, a later rewrite having to beat it by more than 9.41%. The loop stops when the planner declines to revise, when a revision does not lower the best product by more than 9.41%, when a revision fails its checks, or when 9 revisions have been made.

Stated: the BLOCKS, TILES and STAGE_NS lines of the plan header. Measured: the packed DSP tile count from the gate flow, and the median period, area and wirelength over the seeds. "A/A0 · D/D0 · W/W0" are the rewrite's medians over the baseline's, whose product is the "vs baseline" change plus one. "vs previous" is against the rewrite measured before this one. "Path 1 ends in" is read from the rewrite's own timing report and netlist: the constant coefficients on the block (or plain multiply) that path 1 passes through, matched against the constants each module of the edited RTL multiplies by; two modules that share a coefficient set are both named, and the hover text gives the element and its constants. Verification comes from verification.yaml in the run dir when one was written; the loop itself does not run the equivalence checks. Its label is proven when the LEC closed, simulation under assumption when the simulation passed without a closed proof and the plan stated a bound it rests on, simulation only when it stated none; the hover text gives the simulation and LEC results and the stated bounds.
